registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: Patients affected by histologically proven rectal cancer were considered for enrollment in a prospective protocol that included preoperative CRT and surgical treatment. All patients underwent pre-treatment work-up (clinical examination, pancolonoscopy with biopsy, total body CT scan, pelvic MRI, and whole body 18-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT scan). Eligible patients had primary resectable cT2-low lying-T3, N0-N1 adenocarcinoma of the rectum, without evidence of disease in lateral lymph nodes. Additional eligibility criteria included performance status as well as liver, kidney, and bone marrow function that allowed for long-course CRT, older than 18 years, and no distant metastases.

registry_schema.text: The purpose of this study is to determine the ability of hyperthermia (heat treatments produced by sound waves) when combined with radiation therapy and in some patients hormonal therapy to control prostate cancer. Hyperthermia refers to the use of temperatures 42 oC (107-6oF) or higher to treatment malignant tumors. Laboratory and some clinical reports have demonstrated a tumor killing effect if tumors are heated to 43oC (109oF) for 30-60 minutes. schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-center phase 2, 1:1 randomized, investigator-blinded, non-inferiority trial of hypofractionated versus standard definitive chemoradiotherapy for uterine cervix cancer.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Biopsy-proven squamous, adeno, or adenosquamous cervix cancer, FIGO 2018 IIA to IIIC1, age 18-85, eligible for cisplatin, ECOG 0-2.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Permuted blocks of 6, stratified by FIGO stage.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Both arms receive external-beam radiotherapy, weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2, a node boost for stage IIIC1, and brachytherapy 28 Gy in 4 weekly fractions starting 1 week after external-beam radiotherapy. The reported interim cohort used 3D conformal radiotherapy.

arms.label: Hypofractionated
arms.text: 40 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks with 3 weekly cisplatin doses. Stage IIIC1 receives an additional 8 Gy in 3 fractions to gross nodes.

arms.label: Standard
arms.text: 45 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks with up to 5 weekly cisplatin doses. Stage IIIC1 receives an additional 9 Gy in 5 fractions to gross nodes.

brief.schema_source: The open-access interim report states the stage-stratified randomization, external-beam doses, cisplatin schedule, node boosts, and brachytherapy.
eligibility: Age 18 to 85, biopsy-proven squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, or adenosquamous carcinoma, FIGO 2018 stage IIA to IIIC1 on MRI, medically eligible for cisplatin, ECOG 0 to 2, and written consent.

Excluded: inflammatory bowel disease, connective-tissue disease, prior pelvic radiotherapy or hysterectomy. Stage IIIB with hydronephrosis was excluded if creatinine clearance was below 30 mL/min. Stage IIIC1 was excluded for more than three MRI nodes, any node with short-axis 3 cm or larger, or common iliac lymphadenopathy.

eligibility: Age 18 or older. ECOG 0-2.
Triple-negative breast cancer: ER and PR 10% or less, HER2-negative by ASCO/CAP (IHC and FISH). If both breasts had invasive disease, both must meet criteria.
Clinical stage T1bN1-2 or T2-4N0-2 (stage II-III) before preoperative therapy, AJCC 8th edition.
pCR: no residual invasive disease in breast or nodes after neoadjuvant therapy. Residual DCIS allowed. Isolated tumor cells count as node-negative.
Neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab for at least 6 cycles, with all chemotherapy completed preoperatively.

No more than 12 weeks from final surgery to randomization. Adjuvant pembrolizumab before entry is discouraged; if given, no more than 6 weeks post-surgery and completed before registration. Investigational anti-cancer agents stopped by registration.

Adequate excision: total mastectomy, or breast-conserving surgery with negative margins (no ink on tumor, including DCIS). Persistent DCIS at the margin after re-excision requires mastectomy. LCIS at the margin is allowed.

Axilla: clinically N0 needs sentinel node biopsy; a positive post-treatment sentinel node makes the patient ineligible. Biopsy-proven N1 at diagnosis needs post-treatment axillary surgery; a positive pre-treatment sentinel node requires ALND after preoperative therapy.
Breast-conserving surgery patients must be planned to receive breast radiation.
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test within 7 days before randomization).

ANC at least 1,000/mm3, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, eGFR at least 15 mL/min/1.73 m2, total bilirubin at most 1.5 x ULN (Gilbert's up to 2.5 x ULN with normal direct bilirubin), AST/ALT at most 3 x ULN.
No stage IV disease and no evidence of recurrence after preoperative therapy and surgery.
No prior invasive breast cancer (ipsilateral or contralateral). Prior DCIS allowed. Other prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
No known active liver disease (HBV, HCV, autoimmune hepatitis, sclerosing cholangitis). HIV allowed if on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months before registration.
Known cardiac disease or prior cardiotoxic therapy: NYHA class 2B or better.

No grade 3-4 infusion reaction or hypersensitivity to pembrolizumab, murine proteins, or product components. Prior irAEs allowed if resolved to grade 1 or less without chronic steroids; grade 2 or lower endocrinopathies stable on replacement are allowed.
No condition requiring chronic systemic steroids (more than 10 mg prednisone daily or equivalent) or other immunosuppression within the last 2 years. Physiologic replacement is allowed.
Diagnostic core biopsy tissue requested; inadequate tissue does not exclude.

eligibility: Age 18 or older. ECOG 0-2.

pCR: no residual invasive disease in breast or nodes. Residual DCIS allowed. Residual isolated tumor cells count as node-positive and are not eligible.

Neoadjuvant chemotherapy with trastuzumab +/- pertuzumab for at least 12 weeks, all chemotherapy completed preoperatively. At least 12 and no more than 24 weeks of total trastuzumab coverage (neoadjuvant plus adjuvant) before registration.

Prior endocrine therapy for DCIS or prevention must have stopped more than 12 months before registration if endocrine therapy is indicated now. Endocrine therapy for the current cancer before registration is allowed.

Adequate excision: mastectomy with grossly negative margins, or breast-conserving surgery with no ink on tumor (including DCIS) unless the margin is at skin or chest wall and cannot be re-excised. Nodal surgery required (SLNB, targeted axillary dissection, or ALND).

Breast-conserving surgery patients must have received or plan to receive adjuvant RT. Not eligible if RT is indicated but medically contraindicated (for example, connective tissue disorder or prior ipsilateral breast RT).
LVEF 50% or higher on most recent echo or MUGA (within 90 days before registration).
Not pregnant and not nursing. No required laboratory thresholds; organ function adequate for HER2 therapy per investigator.
No stage IV disease and no recurrence after preoperative therapy and surgery.
No prior invasive breast cancer (ipsilateral or contralateral). Prior DCIS allowed. Other prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
No grade 3-4 toxicity from trastuzumab, or from pertuzumab if pertuzumab is planned. No contraindication to further HER2-directed therapy.
HIV allowed if healthy with low risk of AIDS-related illness. HBV or HCV allowed if healthy and otherwise eligible.
No severe uncontrolled systemic disease that could interfere with planned therapy.

eligibility: Step 0 requires a well- or moderately differentiated bronchial neuroendocrine tumor, reported as well- or moderately differentiated neuroendocrine tumor, low- or intermediate-grade neuroendocrine tumor, or typical or atypical carcinoid, from the primary or a metastasis.

Functional and nonfunctional tumors are allowed, and poorly differentiated or high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma, including large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma and small-cell lung cancer, and mixed tumors such as adenocarcinoid, are excluded.
Disease is recurrent, locally advanced unresectable, or metastatic, with radiologic progression in the 12 months before pre-registration.

SSTR PET, preferably 68Ga-DOTATATE, must be positive in the 12 months before pre-registration, with uptake greater than background liver in every measurable lesion, and documentation within 6 months is preferred.
Step 1 requires central confirmation of that SSTR positivity by the Alliance ICL at IROC Ohio.

Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 on CT or MRI is required, at least 1 cm, or at least 1.5 cm in short axis for nodes, and a lesion treated with percutaneous therapy or radiotherapy counts only if it has clearly progressed.

Treatment-naive and previously treated patients are allowed, previously treated disease must have progressed on that therapy, and prior peptide-receptor radionuclide therapy and prior mTOR inhibitors are excluded.

Prior hepatic-artery embolization or ablation is allowed if measurable disease remains outside the treated area or a treated site has progressed, liver-directed therapy must finish at least 28 days before registration, and yttrium-90 radioembolization must finish at least 6 weeks before.

Lung or mediastinal stereotactic radiotherapy must finish at least 14 days before registration and conventional radiotherapy at least 28 days before, systemic anticancer therapy and major surgery must finish at least 28 days before with wound healing complete, and prior toxicity should be grade 1 or less except alopecia, fatigue, and irreversible effects such as cisplatin neuropathy.

A somatostatin analog may continue only for a functional tumor that already progressed radiographically on a somatostatin analog, and P-gp or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers must stop 7 days before registration.

Age is 18 or older, ECOG performance status is 0-2, and patients are not pregnant and not nursing, with a negative pregnancy test within 28 days before registration for women of childbearing potential.

Labs are hemoglobin at least 8.0 g/dL, platelets at least 75,000/mm3, ANC at least 1,500/mm3, creatinine at most 1.5 x ULN or Cockcroft-Gault clearance at least 40 mL/min, total bilirubin at most 2.0 x ULN, albumin at least 2.8 g/dL, and AST or ALT at most 3.0 x ULN.
If Gilbert syndrome and total bilirubin is above 2.0 x ULN, direct bilirubin must be at most 2.0 x ULN.

CNS metastases must be treated and clinically stable for at least 14 days, with weaning steroids if steroids are used, and no other active malignancy is expected to need therapy during the study except non-melanoma skin cancer and in situ carcinoma such as breast or cervical.

Known active hepatitis B is excluded unless the viral load is undetectable on suppression, known active hepatitis C with detectable HCV RNA is excluded, and HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months of registration is allowed.

Active infection requiring antifungals or antibiotics in the prior 3 days, a live attenuated vaccine in the prior 7 days, decompensated cirrhosis, prior symptomatic or treated drug-induced pneumonitis, inability to swallow, impaired absorption of an oral agent, and hypersensitivity to everolimus or another rapamycin analog are exclusions.

Re-registration for crossover requires centrally confirmed RECIST progression, ECOG 0-2, the same laboratory thresholds, and a negative pregnancy test within 28 days for women of childbearing potential.

publications.title: Alliance for clinical trials in Oncology (Alliance) trial A022101/NRG-GI009: a pragmatic randomized phase III trial evaluating total ablative therapy for patients with limited metastatic colorectal cancer: evaluating radiation, ablation, and surgery (ERASur).
Oligometastatic Colorectal Cancer: A Review of Definitions and Patient Selection for Local Therapies.

schema.label: Initial systemic therapy
schema.text: Newly diagnosed limited metastatic colorectal cancer receives physician-choice systemic therapy for at least 12 weeks and at most 52 weeks before registration. A 5-FU cycle is 14 days, a capecitabine cycle is 14 or 21 days, and a total-ablative-therapy cycle is 90 days. Patients may pre-register before or during that chemotherapy, or pre-register and register together after 12 weeks.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Institutional standard-of-care therapy before progression, including added systemic therapy, maintenance, a treatment pause, or restart, counts as on-protocol treatment. Patients are followed for 5 years or until death. Surgery, microwave ablation, and radiotherapy of metastatic sites are done at the registering institution. Chemotherapy may be given elsewhere.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Total ablative therapy, then institutional standard-of-care therapy. Total ablative therapy may be SBRT, microwave ablation, surgical resection, or any combination.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Institutional standard-of-care therapy, which may include more systemic therapy, maintenance chemotherapy, or a treatment pause, as the treating physician decides.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Overall survival from randomization, comparing total ablative therapy plus standard-of-care systemic therapy with standard-of-care systemic therapy in newly diagnosed oligometastatic colorectal cancer.

eligibility: Step 0 requires pathologically proven colorectal adenocarcinoma with metastases, from a primary or metastatic biopsy, with no known microsatellite instability and no known BRAF V600E mutation.

Treated brain metastases are allowed if follow-up brain imaging shows no progression, known peritoneal or omental metastases are excluded, and liver-only disease on baseline imaging before chemotherapy is not allowed.
Patients with liver metastases must have at least one other metastatic site on initial imaging, and they remain eligible if later imaging after systemic therapy shows liver-only disease.
Measurable disease by RECIST 1.1 is required at pre-registration and at registration.
Step 1 requires no overt progression during pre-registration systemic therapy, and the patient is not eligible for hepatic artery infusion pump therapy or the benefit of that therapy is undefined.

The primary tumor is already resected, a rectal primary has had a clinical complete response without resection and no local regrowth, or a surgeon or multidisciplinary tumor board judges the primary resectable; an unresectable primary is not eligible.

After at least 12 weeks of systemic therapy there are 4 or fewer apparent metastatic sites, not counting the primary or regional nodes, each radiographically evident and amenable to resection, microwave ablation, SABR, or a combination.

One site means each hemiliver, each lung lobe, each adrenal gland, nodes treatable in one resection or one SABR field, or bone metastases treatable in one SABR field, and lung nodules smaller than 5 mm count as metastases unless they were stable for more than 2 months before systemic therapy.

First-line systemic therapy for metastatic disease lasts at least 12 weeks and at most 52 weeks, and prior definitive therapy, including adjuvant chemotherapy, must have finished at least 6 months before the metastatic diagnosis.

Age is 18 or older, ECOG performance status is 0-2, and patients are not pregnant and not nursing, with a negative pregnancy test within 14 days before registration for women of childbearing potential.

Labs are ANC at least 1,000/mm3, platelets at least 50,000/mm3, creatinine at most 1.5 x ULN or Cockcroft-Gault clearance at least 30 mL/min, total bilirubin at most 1.5 x ULN, and AST or ALT at most 3.0 x ULN, or at most 5 x ULN with metastatic liver disease.
In Gilbert disease, direct bilirubin replaces total bilirubin and must be at most 1.5 ULN if FOLFIRI is planned and at most 3.0 x ULN if mFOLFOX6 is planned.

Patients with known cardiac disease, cardiac symptoms, or prior cardiotoxic therapy should be class 2B or better, a prior or concurrent malignancy is allowed if it would not interfere with assessment, HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is allowed without required HIV testing, and no other concurrent investigational agent is planned.

calendar.window: To be completed ≤ 28 DAYS before registration: Scan of any type which is used for tumor measurement per protocol. All laboratory studies and history and physical. Baseline imaging must have been obtained ≤ 90 days prior to initiation of systemic therapy

schema.text: 240 mg IV Day 1 of each cycle before chemotherapy. Mandatory for CPS 5 or higher unless contraindicated; physician choice for CPS less than 5. Allowed after prior early-stage immunotherapy if the last dose was at least 1 year before registration.

eligibility: Age 18 or older. ECOG 0-1.

Unresectable or metastatic adenocarcinoma of the esophagus, GEJ, or stomach. HER2-negative by ASCO/CAP, with PD-L1 expression known before registration (CPS preferred; TPS or laboratory-developed tests acceptable; any level allowed).
Measurable or non-measurable but evaluable disease by RECIST 1.1.
No prior systemic therapy for unresectable or metastatic disease. Prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy or adjuvant immunotherapy allowed if completed at least 1 year before registration.

ANC at least 1,500/mm3, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, creatinine at most 1.5 x ULN or CrCl at least 30 mL/min, total bilirubin at most 1.5 x ULN, AST/ALT at most 3 x ULN (at most 5 x ULN if due to liver metastases).
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test within 7 days before registration).
No known Gilbert's syndrome or known UGT1A1*28 homozygosity.
No baseline grade 2 or higher peripheral neuropathy, neurosensory, or neuromotor toxicity.

No untreated symptomatic brain metastases. Treated brain metastases allowed if imaging at least 4 weeks after CNS therapy shows no progression and the patient is off steroids or on a stable dose for more than 4 weeks.
Cardiac disease or prior cardiotoxic therapy: NYHA class 2B or better. No uncontrolled infection or diabetes that makes protocol therapy unreasonably hazardous.
HIV allowed if on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months of registration.
No allogeneic tissue or organ transplant. Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

If nivolumab is planned: no active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment within 6 months (vitiligo, type 1 diabetes, hormone-replaced hypothyroidism, and psoriasis not needing systemic therapy are allowed); no steroids above 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent or other immunosuppression within 14 days; no noninfectious pneumonitis requiring steroids; no prior immune-related adverse event that led to permanent immunotherapy discontinuation.

schema.label: Registration by histology cohort
schema.text: Single-arm phase II with parallel cohorts: A small cell/neuroendocrine bladder; B bladder, urachal, or bladder/urethra clear cell adenocarcinoma; C squamous cell bladder; D plasmacytoid urothelial; E any penile cancer; F sarcomatoid RCC; G miscellaneous GU variants; H sarcomatoid urothelial; I renal medullary; J bone-only non-prostate GU (exploratory); K collecting duct; L urethral. Expansion cohorts (checkpoint-inhibitor naive only) added for A, C, and L in Update #07.

schema.label: Cycles 1-4: triplet (21-day cycles)
schema.text: Cabozantinib 40 mg PO daily, nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Day 1, ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Day 1, every 3 weeks for 4 doses. Treatment starts within 14 days of registration.

schema.label: Cycle 5 onward: doublet (28-day cycles)
schema.text: Cabozantinib 40 mg PO daily plus nivolumab 480 mg IV Day 1 every 4 weeks, until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

schema.label: Duration
schema.text: With confirmed CR or PR, treatment continues 2 years from response; with stable disease beyond 9 months, total therapy is 33 months. Then surveillance off treatment.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: 5 years from registration or until death.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Objective response rate per cohort. Simon two-stage design: 9 then up to 17 evaluable patients (null 5%, target 30%); expansion of 30 patients if 3 or more responses in 17.

eligibility: Age 18 or older. Karnofsky 80% or higher. Able to swallow tablets.

Histologically confirmed metastatic disease (new or progressive lesions) in one of cohorts A-L, with at least one RECIST 1.1 measurable lesion, or at least one bone lesion for the bone-only cohort J. Pure histology required for adenocarcinoma and squamous cohorts; about 50% or more variant histology for plasmacytoid, sarcomatoid, and micropapillary types.

Treatment-naive or up to 2 prior systemic therapies. Small cell carcinoma must have had a platinum-based combination (neoadjuvant, adjuvant, or first line). Urothelial bone-only patients must have had cisplatin-based chemotherapy if cisplatin-eligible.

No prior PD-1, PD-L1, or CTLA-4 therapy, except urothelial histology cohorts (D, H, J, L). Expansion cohorts enroll checkpoint-naive patients only. No prior cabozantinib; prior MET or VEGFR inhibitor allowed, but not both MET/VEGF and checkpoint therapy.

ANC at least 1,000/mcL, platelets at least 75,000/mcL, hemoglobin at least 9 g/dL (transfusion allowed), albumin at least 3.2 g/dL, total bilirubin at most 1.5 x ULN (Gilbert's up to 3.0 mg/dL), AST/ALT at most 3 x ULN (5 x ULN with liver metastases or Gilbert's), creatinine at most 1.5 x ULN or CrCl at least 40 mL/min/1.73 m2, lipase and amylase at most 2 x ULN with no pancreatitis.

Washouts: no cytotoxic or biologic therapy within 2 weeks; no small-molecule kinase inhibitor or hormonal therapy within 14 days or 5 half-lives (GnRH agonists/antagonists allowed); no investigational agent within 14 days; no radionuclide within 6 weeks. Prior toxicity recovered to grade 1 or less.
No RT to lungs, mediastinum, or abdomen within 4 weeks (or ongoing complications); no WBRT within 3 weeks or SRS within 2 weeks; no RT to other sites within 2 weeks before first dose.
No active brain metastases or epidural disease. Treated brain metastases allowed if asymptomatic and off steroids for at least 2 weeks; resection or biopsy at least 3 months before treatment.
No tumor invading major blood vessels, the GI tract, or the airway (endotracheal or endobronchial) within 28 days. No rectal tumor masses.

No clinically significant GI bleeding within 6 months, hemoptysis of 2.5 mL or more within 1 month, or pulmonary hemorrhage within 3 months. No GI or GU fistula, perforation, obstruction, or intra-abdominal abscess within 2 years; no active diverticulitis, abscess, or GI obstruction within 12 months.

Cardiac: no NYHA class III-IV heart failure; no uncontrolled hypertension (above 150/90 despite treatment); QTcF 500 ms or less; no congenital long QT; no unstable angina, significant arrhythmia (atrial fibrillation allowed), stroke or TIA, MI, or cardiomyopathy within 6 months.
No major surgery within 3 months (6 weeks if healed in aggressive cancers) or minor surgery within 1 month; wounds fully healed. No serious non-healing wound or fracture.
No full-dose warfarin (low-dose warfarin up to 1 mg/day, aspirin up to 325 mg/day, LMWH, and thrombin or factor Xa inhibitors allowed). No chronic strong CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors.

No active autoimmune disease or history that may recur and threaten organ function or need immunosuppression (for example, MS, Guillain-Barre, myasthenia, SLE, IBD, TEN/SJS). Vitiligo, replaced endocrinopathies, and topically controlled psoriasis or arthropathies allowed.
No positive HBsAg (unless PCR negative) or active HCV. HIV allowed on stable HAART with CD4 above 350 and undetectable viral load.
No organ or allogeneic stem cell transplant. No severe hypersensitivity to monoclonal antibodies. No active malignancy requiring systemic therapy within 2 years.
No severe infection needing IV treatment within 14 days and no uncompensated thyroid dysfunction within 7 days.
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test within 7 days before registration).

eligibility: Age 18 or older. ECOG 0-2.

Histologically confirmed muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of the bladder, urethra, ureter, or renal pelvis. Variant histology allowed if urothelial is predominant; not pure squamous cell carcinoma.

Radical cystectomy with lymph node dissection, nephroureterectomy, or ureterectomy. Not eligible after partial cystectomy as definitive therapy. No gross margin disease (microscopic positive margins allowed; CIS at margin counts as negative). No residual disease or metastasis.

After neoadjuvant therapy (cisplatin-based, cisplatin plus PD-1/PD-L1, or enfortumab vedotin plus PD-1/PD-L1), ypT2-T4N0/Nx or ypTanyN+.
Signatera pathway: commercial result from blood drawn 3-16 weeks after surgery (16-target, exome-designed assay), or central testing with samples submitted 3-12 weeks after surgery.

Step 1: registration within 18 weeks of surgery; evaluable ctDNA result; disease-free on imaging within 60 days (equivocal nodes under 15 mm short axis or non-nodal lesions under 10 mm allowed). Upper-tract primaries must have no high-grade urothelial cancer in the bladder.
No adjuvant systemic therapy or adjuvant radiation after radical surgery. No investigational agent within 4 weeks of pre-registration. No prior LAG-3 blockade.

ANC at least 1,200/mm3, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin at least 8 g/dL, creatinine at most 1.5 x ULN or CrCl above 30 mL/min, AST/ALT at most 3 x ULN, total bilirubin at most 1.5 x ULN (Gilbert's below 3.0 mg/dL).
Not on hemodialysis. No current or prior myocarditis.
No grade 3 or higher immune-related adverse event with prior neoadjuvant PD-1/PD-L1 blockade.

No active or recurrence-prone autoimmune disease that may affect vital organs or require immunosuppression (vitiligo, type 1 diabetes, replaced endocrinopathies allowed). No pneumonitis requiring steroids within 5 years.

No active HBV or HCV. Chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load; HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment. HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
No concurrent antineoplastic or anti-hormonal cancer therapy. No steroids above 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent or other immunosuppression within 14 days of pre-registration.
No major surgery within 3 weeks and no live vaccine within 30 days before registration.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment. Not pregnant and not nursing.
Step 2 (Arm 4 only): central conversion to ctDNA(+), no metastatic disease on the most recent scheduled imaging, and fit for nivolumab.

Histologically or cytologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma without small cell histology.

M1 disease on conventional CT/MRI and/or bone scan: bone metastases (PCWG3), non-regional nodes above the aortic bifurcation (short axis 15 mm or more), or visceral/soft tissue lesions. Regional (N1) nodes only, or PSMA-PET-only disease, are not eligible.
No metachronous low-volume disease (recurrence after definitive local therapy with 4 or fewer bone metastases and no visceral disease).
Tissue-based CLIA NGS result available at registration (soft tissue or visceral preferred; bone or primary accepted; blood-based not allowed). Failed NGS is not eligible.
ADT (LHRH agonist/antagonist or orchiectomy), with or without a first-generation anti-androgen or ARSI, only if started within 120 days of registration. No prior chemotherapy for prostate cancer.

ANC at least 1,500/mm3, hemoglobin at least 9.0 g/dL, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, total bilirubin at most 1 x ULN (Gilbert's eligible if direct bilirubin at most 1 x ULN), AST/ALT at most 1.5 x ULN, CrCl above 30 mL/min.
No seizure or seizure-predisposing condition (stroke within 1 year, brain AVM, or condition needing CNS surgery or RT). Seizure-threshold-lowering drugs stopped before entry.
Treated leptomeningeal metastases allowed if brain imaging 30 days after CNS therapy shows no progression.
Cardiac disease or prior cardiotoxic therapy: NYHA class II or better. Stable asymptomatic DVT on anticoagulation allowed.
No uncontrolled hypertension (resting systolic 160 or diastolic 100 mmHg despite treatment).
HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months. Chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load; HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment.
No chronic strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (stop before registration) or strong inducers (stop 14 days before treatment). No hypersensitivity to study drugs.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

schema.label: Step 0
schema.text: Two doses of lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy. Patients whose PSA falls by at least 50% after those two cycles continue to randomization. Patients without that decline, and any other patient who does not move to Step 1, are treated at investigator discretion and are not followed.

schema.label: Step 1 randomize 1:1
schema.text: Each lutetium dose in the treatment plan is 7.4 GBq plus or minus 10% (200 mCi). Treatment continues until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Patients are followed for 5 years or until death. A trigger for the adaptive arm is an absolute PSA rise of at least 4 ng/dL, a PSA rise of at least 25% above nadir, radiographic progression by PCWG3, or clinical progression. The schema prints the absolute rise as ng/dL.

arms.label: Arm 1: standard dosing
arms.text: The next lutetium dose is scheduled in 3 weeks, then doses 3 through 6 are given every 6 weeks, plus or minus 1 week.

arms.label: Arm 2: adaptive dosing
arms.text: PSA is checked every 3 weeks starting on cycle 2, day 42, plus or minus 7 days. If no trigger is met, PSA checks continue every 3 weeks. If a PSA rise or clinical progression is met, the next dose is scheduled for 3 weeks later, plus or minus 1 week, and PSA monitoring resumes after that dose. This continues until doses 3 through 6 are given or disease progresses.

schema.label: Co-primary endpoints
schema.text: Overall survival for PSA-adaptive lutetium dosing compared with standard dosing every 6 weeks, and quality of life by FACT-P total score averaged over the first 30 months.

eligibility: Step 0 requires prostate adenocarcinoma confirmed by histology, pathology, or cytology, and progressive metastatic castration-resistant disease.
PSMA PET/CT with 68Ga-PSMA-11, 18F-DCFPyL, or 18F-rhPSMA-7.3 must show uptake greater than liver and no PSMA-negative measurable soft-tissue disease, and PSA must be greater than 2.0 ng/mL.

Progression is two consecutive PSA rises over a reference value from at least 1 week earlier, with a minimum start value of 2.0 ng/mL, or soft-tissue growth of at least 20% in the sum of diameters from the nadir sum or a new lesion, or bone progression by 2+2 PCWG3 criteria.

Prior orchiectomy or ongoing androgen deprivation is required, with testosterone below 50 ng/dL or below 1.7 nmol/L, and at least one of apalutamide, darolutamide, enzalutamide, or abiraterone is required and must stop at least 4 weeks before pre-registration.

Taxane chemotherapy for mCRPC is excluded, docetaxel for metastatic hormone-sensitive disease or neoadjuvant or adjuvant use is allowed if completed at least 12 months before pre-registration, and clinically significant prior toxicity must have recovered to grade 2 or less.

A stable bisphosphonate or denosumab regimen for at least 30 days is allowed, and strontium-89, samarium-153, rhenium-186, rhenium-188, radium-223, hemi-body irradiation within 6 months, and any prior PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy are excluded.

Systemic anticancer therapy and investigational agents within 28 days, and transfusion within 30 days before pre-registration, are excluded, and there is no concurrent cytotoxic chemotherapy, immunotherapy, radioligand therapy, or investigational therapy.

Age is 18 or older, ECOG performance status is 2 or better, there is no acute biliary or urinary obstruction and no symptomatic or impending cord compression, and the patient can read and comprehend English or Spanish.

Treated brain metastases are allowed if follow-up imaging shows no progression, the patient is neurologically stable and asymptomatic, and corticosteroids are not used to maintain neurologic function; treated stable epidural or canal disease without deficit is allowed, and parenchymal CNS disease requires brain MRI or contrast CT.

HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months is allowed, hepatitis B must be undetectable on suppression if indicated, hepatitis C must be cured or undetectable on treatment, and there is no known hypersensitivity to the study therapy or its analogs.
Patients with known cardiac disease or prior cardiotoxic therapy should be NYHA class II or better, and myocardial infarction, CABG, or angina within 6 months before pre-registration is excluded.

Step 0 labs are ANC at least 1,500/mm3, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin at least 9.0 g/dL, total bilirubin below 1.5 x ULN or below 3 x ULN in Gilbert syndrome, eGFR at least 40 mL/min/1.73 m2 by MDRD, and ALT or AST at most 3.0 x ULN without liver metastases or at most 5.0 x ULN with liver metastases.

Step 1 requires two completed doses of lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy, a PSA decline of at least 50% from cycle 1 day 1 to cycle 2 day 22 plus or minus 3 days, ECOG 2 or better, and repeat ANC, platelet, eGFR, and ALT or AST thresholds, with hemoglobin at least 9 g/dL and transfusions allowed; Step 1 does not restate a bilirubin limit.

amendments.text: Update #10, the current version. Phase III enrollment was closed earlier, in Update 08, when the Pilot Cohort became the only enrolling arm.

schema.label: Enrollment status
schema.text: As of Update 08 the phase III randomization is permanently closed to new patients, and all new patients enroll on the single-arm Pilot Cohort (planned 24 patients). The confirmation of tolerability phase was completed in 2018 at inotuzumab 0.5 mg/m2 on Days 1, 8, and 15 of a 28-day cycle.

schema.label: Step 0: Pre-registration
schema.text: Baseline bone marrow (or peripheral blood if inaspirable) sent centrally. For the closed phase III this included the LDA assay used for stratification.

schema.label: Step 1: Registration, Course I induction
schema.text: C10403 pediatric-inspired induction starting within 5 days of registration: IT cytarabine Day 1; dexamethasone Days 1-7 and 15-21; vincristine and daunorubicin 25 mg/m2 Days 1, 8, 15, 22; pegaspargase (age over 21.5) or calaspargase (age under 21.5) once Day 4-6; IT methotrexate Days 8 and 29 (also Days 15 and 22 for CNS3). Day 29 bone marrow. M3 or M4 marrow (more than 25% blasts) ends protocol treatment, with survival follow-up every 6 months.

schema.label: Pilot Cohort (current)
schema.text: M2 or better marrow: one 28-day cycle of inotuzumab ozogamicin 0.5 mg/m2 IV Days 1, 8, 15 (1.5 mg/m2 per cycle), then Course II consolidation, one 6-week cycle of blinatumomab (28 mcg/day continuous infusion Days 1-28), Course III interim maintenance, a second blinatumomab cycle, Course IV delayed intensification, then Course V maintenance.

schema.label: Step 2: Randomize 1:1 (phase III, closed)
schema.text: Stratified by age (25 or younger vs older than 25), Day 29 marrow (M0/M1 vs M2), CD20 status, and LDA card (BCR-ABL1-like vs not vs not evaluable). Randomization within 21 days after induction.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: C10403 backbone: Course II consolidation, Course III interim maintenance, Course IV delayed intensification, Course V maintenance.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Two 28-day cycles of inotuzumab 0.5 mg/m2 Days 1, 8, 15, then the same C10403 Courses II-V.

schema.label: Backbone courses
schema.text: Course II (8 weeks): cyclophosphamide 1000 mg/m2 Days 1 and 29, cytarabine, 6-mercaptopurine, vincristine, asparaginase, IT methotrexate, plus rituximab 375 mg/m2 for CD20-positive disease. Course III: Capizzi escalating IV methotrexate with vincristine, asparaginase, and IT methotrexate. Course IV: dexamethasone, vincristine, doxorubicin 25 mg/m2, asparaginase, then cyclophosphamide, cytarabine, and thioguanine. Course V: 12-week cycles of vincristine, dexamethasone pulses, daily 6-mercaptopurine, weekly oral methotrexate, and IT methotrexate, until 2 years (women) or 3 years (men) from the start of interim maintenance.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: CNS3 patients in CR: cranial RT 18 Gy in 10 fractions during the first cycle of Course V. Testicular disease at diagnosis not resolved by end of induction: testicular RT 24 Gy in 12 fractions during Course II.

schema.label: MRD-positive patients
schema.text: MRD 0.1% or higher after inotuzumab, Course II, or any later marrow: blinatumomab up to 4 cycles, then subsequent treatment at investigator discretion.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Phase III: event-free survival without censoring for transplant. Pilot: safety and tolerability of one inotuzumab cycle plus two blinatumomab cycles added to C10403.

eligibility: Newly diagnosed CD22-positive precursor B-cell ALL (WHO). CD22 and CD20 positivity means expression on more than 20% of blasts by local flow cytometry.
No Burkitt-type ALL. No BCR-ABL fusion by FISH or RT-PCR and no t(9;22)(q34;q11) by cytogenetics.

No prior therapy for ALL except up to 7 days of corticosteroids or hydroxyurea (including emergency therapy for blast crisis, SVC syndrome, or renal failure from leukemic infiltration) and a single dose of IT cytarabine. Systemic chemotherapy must start within 72 hours of that IT dose. Chronic steroids for other conditions are allowed.
Age 18 or older and younger than 40. ECOG performance status 0-2.
No Down syndrome.
AST and ALT 3 x ULN or less and direct bilirubin 3 x ULN or less, unless leukemic liver involvement is suspected. Creatinine clearance 50 mL/min or higher by Cockcroft-Gault.
Not pregnant and not nursing. Pregnancy test within 8 days before registration for women of childbearing potential.

HIV is allowed if no AIDS-related complications other than prior low CD4 count, HIV viral load under 200 copies/mm3 on combination antiretroviral therapy compatible with protocol therapy (no cobicistat, stavudine, or zidovudine).
No currently active second malignancy other than non-melanoma skin cancer or cervical carcinoma in situ (3 or more years disease-free after therapy is not considered active).
Must be able to swallow oral medications.

Step 2 (phase III, closed): completed induction with M2 marrow or better (25% blasts or less), ANC 750/mm3 or higher, platelets 75,000/mm3 or higher, total bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less (except Gilbert syndrome), and AST 8 x ULN or less.

schema.label: Step 0: Pre-registration
schema.text: Mandatory first-pull bone marrow aspirate and peripheral blood to the HEME Biobank for MRD. Protocol treatment starts within 7 days of registration.

schema.label: Cohort 1
schema.text: Newly diagnosed Ph-negative CD22-positive B-ALL, age 60 or older, not planned for HCT. Induction Course IA: inotuzumab ozogamicin 0.8 mg/m2 Day 1 and 0.5 mg/m2 Days 8 and 15 (21 days), marrow Day 18-21. CR/CRi: Course IB, inotuzumab 0.5 mg/m2 Days 1, 8, 15 (28 days). Adequate cytoreduction without CR (50% or greater blast reduction or marrow cellularity 20% or less): Course IC, 0.8/0.5/0.5 mg/m2 (28 days). Inadequate cytoreduction goes straight to Course II. Then Course II blinatumomab (84 days), then Course IIIA (two 42-day blinatumomab cycles) after CR/CRi to induction, or Course IIIB (three 42-day cycles) if induction did not produce CR/CRi.

schema.label: Cohort 2
schema.text: Relapsed or refractory Ph-negative CD22-positive B-ALL in salvage 1 or 2, age 18 or older. Same inotuzumab induction (Courses IA, IB, or IC) and Course II blinatumomab, then Course IIIB blinatumomab (126 days) if in CR/CRi. Allogeneic HCT is allowed any time after CR/CRi.

schema.label: Cohort 3 (feasibility)
schema.text: Newly diagnosed Ph/BCR-ABL1-positive CD22-positive B-ALL, age 75 or older, or 18 or older and HyperCVAD-ineligible. Course I (35 days): ponatinib 45 mg daily, dexamethasone 20 mg/m2 Days 1-7 and 15-21, IT methotrexate Days 1, 15, 29. Course IIA (21 days): ponatinib 15 mg (if CMR) or 30 mg with inotuzumab 0.3 mg/m2 Days 1, 8, 15 if in CR/CRi, or 0.6/0.3/0.3 mg/m2 if not. Course IIB (CR/CRi after IIA) or IIC (no CR/CRi): one more 28-day inotuzumab cycle with ponatinib. Courses III and IV: two 42-day blinatumomab cycles each with ponatinib. Maintenance: ponatinib 15 mg daily (CMR) or 30 mg daily (no CMR) for 24 months. Ponatinib continues without breaks through maintenance.

schema.label: Blinatumomab dosing
schema.text: Continuous infusion 9 mcg/day Days 1-7 of the first cycle, then 28 mcg/day for 28 days of each 42-day cycle (BSA-based doses if weight under 45 kg). Hospital admission recommended for initiation and cycle restarts.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Cohorts 1 and 2: 1-year event-free survival. Cohort 3: feasibility of the regimen. The confirmation of tolerability lead-in for Cohorts 1 and 2 was completed as of Update #03.

eligibility: Morphologic precursor B-cell ALL (WHO), CD22 on 20% or more of lymphoblasts by local hematopathology. Ph/BCR-ABL1 status by cytogenetics, FISH, or PCR determines cohort (negative for Cohorts 1 and 2, positive for Cohort 3). No Burkitt lymphoma/leukemia.

No active CNS leukemia: only CNS-1 allowed. No CNS-directed treatment for active disease or symptomatic CNS leukemia within 28 days, and no parenchymal CNS mass. Prophylactic IT therapy alone is allowed.
Known or suspected testicular involvement is allowed only with concomitant scrotal/testicular radiotherapy (section 3.3.1); the schema summary instead lists testicular involvement as an exclusion.
ECOG performance status 0-2. Not pregnant and not nursing; pregnancy test within 7 days before registration.

No unstable cardiac disease (MI, angina, uncontrolled heart failure or arrhythmia) within 6 months. No LVEF under 45% or NYHA class III-IV heart failure. No clinically significant ventricular arrhythmia, unexplained non-vasovagal syncope, or chronic bradycardic states unless a permanent pacemaker is in place. QTcF 470 msec or less.

HIV allowed on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months. HBV allowed only on suppressive therapy with no active virus or liver damage. HCV allowed only after eradication with undetectable viral load and no liver damage.

No clinically relevant neurologic disorder (epilepsy, seizure, aphasia, stroke, severe brain injury, structural brain abnormality, benign brain tumor, dementia, Parkinson disease, movement or cerebellar disorder).
No other malignancy except treated basal or squamous cell skin cancer, cervical carcinoma in situ, stage I-II cancer in complete remission, or any cancer disease-free for 2 years or more.
No chronic liver disease or cirrhosis, and no history of SOS/VOD. No uncontrolled infection, and no deep tissue infection (fasciitis, osteomyelitis) within 4 months.
Total bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less (2 x ULN or less for Gilbert disease or leukemic infiltration), AST and ALT 2.5 x ULN or less, creatinine clearance 40 mL/min or higher.

Cohort 1: age 60 or older, Ph-negative, no plan for allogeneic or autologous HCT, and no prior ALL therapy except single-dose IT chemotherapy, corticosteroids, hydroxyurea, or leukapheresis for no more than 14 days, completed at least 24 hours before protocol therapy.

Cohort 2: age 18 or older, Ph-negative, relapsed or refractory in salvage 1 or 2, no isolated extramedullary relapse. Prior allogeneic HCT allowed if 4 months or more before registration, no GVHD, and off immunosuppression for 30 days or more. No prior inotuzumab, blinatumomab, or other CD22- or CD19-directed therapy. Rituximab completed 7 days or more and other monoclonal antibodies 6 weeks or more before registration.

Cohort 2: other prior ALL therapy completed 14 days or more before registration, except IT chemotherapy, hydroxyurea, corticosteroids, 6-mercaptopurine, methotrexate, vincristine, or leukapheresis (completed at least 24 hours before protocol therapy). Prior non-hematologic toxicity resolved to grade 1 or less. Peripheral blast count 10,000/uL or less.

Cohort 3: age 75 or older, or 18 or older and ineligible for HyperCVAD; Ph/BCR-ABL1-positive; no prior ALL therapy except single-dose IT chemotherapy, corticosteroids, hydroxyurea, a BCR-ABL1 TKI, or leukapheresis for no more than 14 days, completed at least 24 hours before protocol therapy. No chronic strong CYP3A4 inducers.

schema.label: Step 0: Pre-registration
schema.text: Mandatory bone marrow or peripheral blood submission to Adaptive (clonoSEQ) for real-time identification of a trackable clone for MRD testing. 1 cycle = 28 days.

schema.label: Step 1: Registration and randomization 1:2
schema.text: Stratified by age (65-74 vs 75 or older), 17p deletion (present if 6.5% or greater by FISH), and IGHV mutation status (>2% vs 2% or less). Treatment starts within 14 days of registration.

arms.label: Arm 1 (Regimen A, control)
arms.text: Zanubrutinib 160 mg PO BID continuously until progression or unacceptable toxicity, up to 10 years. Restaging at C15D1; patients with response continue zanubrutinib.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: Zanubrutinib 160 mg PO BID for cycles 1-3; TLS risk restaging at C3D15; sonrotoclax weekly ramp-up from C4D1 (1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160 mg) to 320 mg daily from C6D1, with zanubrutinib continued, through C15D28. Restaging with peripheral blood MRD at C15D1.

schema.label: Arm 2A
schema.text: Undetectable MRD (<10 residual clonal cells per million nucleated cells), or detectable MRD with response other than PR, PR-L, CR, CCR, or CRi: stop therapy at C15D28.

schema.label: Step 2: Re-randomization 1:1
schema.text: Arm 2 patients with detectable MRD (10 or more residual clonal cells per million) and PR, PR-L, CR, CCR, or CRi.

arms.label: Arm 2B
arms.text: Continue zanubrutinib plus sonrotoclax C16D1 to C27D28 (12 additional cycles), then stop.

arms.label: Arm 2C
arms.text: Stop therapy at C15D28.

schema.label: Co-primary endpoints
schema.text: PFS from initial randomization: (1) MRD-guided Regimen C (Arms 2A+2B) vs continuous zanubrutinib (Arm 1); (2) fixed-duration Regimen B (Arms 2A+2C) vs continuous zanubrutinib. Follow-up up to 10 years.

eligibility: CLL/SLL by IWCLL 2018 criteria: 5 x 10^9/L or more clonal B lymphocytes in blood (CLL) or lymph node biopsy showing SLL; CD19/CD20/CD5-positive clonal B cells; if bright surface immunoglobulin or CD23 absent in >10% of cells, t(11;14) must be absent by FISH.

Meets IWCLL 2018 indication for treatment (progressive marrow failure with Hb <10 g/dL or platelets <100,000/mm3, massive/progressive/symptomatic splenomegaly or lymphadenopathy, poorly responsive autoimmune cytopenia, or constitutional symptoms).

No prior therapy for CLL, except palliative steroids or rituximab/steroids for autoimmune complications, which must be completed before enrollment; palliative steroids no more than 20 mg/day prednisone equivalent at registration.
Age 65 or older; ECOG performance status 0-2.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months before registration. Chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated. HCV must be treated and cured, or undetectable viral load if currently on treatment.
No active systemic anticoagulation with warfarin (off warfarin for at least 5 half-lives with normal INR before enrollment).
Patients with known cardiac disease or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better; acute cardiac events within 6 months need careful evaluation.
No history of severe bleeding disorder, hemorrhagic stroke, or intracranial hemorrhage.
No known active progressive CNS disease.
No known condition preventing swallowing of oral agents.
Step 1: Adaptive report confirming a measurable and trackable B-cell clone.
Step 1: No major surgery within 7 days or minor surgery within 5 days of enrollment.
Step 1: No ongoing active fungal, bacterial, or viral infection requiring systemic therapy (other than the HIV/HBV exceptions), and no uncontrolled systemic infection requiring IV antibiotics.

Step 1: No requirement for more than 20 mg/day prednisone equivalent; no continued need for a strong CYP3A4/5 inhibitor or inducer (stopped at least 14 days or 5 half-lives, whichever is shorter, before first dose).

No ALCL, no CD30 10% or higher, no other subtypes (including large cell transformation of mycosis fungoides). Untreated concurrent B-cell lymphoma related to the T-cell lymphoma is allowed.
Measurable, FDG-avid disease by Lugano criteria.
No prior systemic therapy or radiation therapy for T-cell lymphoma (corticosteroids allowed).
Age 18 or older; ECOG performance status 0-2.
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test within 7 days before registration for women of childbearing potential).
Platelets 75,000/mm3 or more (50,000/mm3 or more if due to marrow involvement, except the first 12 patients per arm, who need 75,000/mm3 or more); ANC 1,000/mm3 or more.

AST and ALT 3.0 x ULN or less (expansion phase exception for liver involvement; 5.0 x ULN or less allowed with liver involvement in the lead-in and safety check); total bilirubin 2.0 x ULN or less unless Gilbert's or liver/pancreatic involvement (expansion phase); creatinine clearance 30 mL/min or more by Cockcroft-Gault.
No known HTLV-1/2 infection and no known CNS involvement.

No active HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C. Seropositive but PCR-negative patients are allowed (HBV-seropositive, DNA-negative patients must take HBV antiviral therapy); cured HCV allowed; HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
No active uncontrolled systemic fungal, bacterial, or viral infection (lymphoma-related EBV viremia allowed).

No concurrent malignancy requiring active therapy within the last 3 years, except skin basal or squamous cell carcinoma, carcinoma in situ of cervix or breast, or localized prostate cancer; adjuvant hormonal therapy after curative treatment allowed.
LVEF 45% or more. No significant cardiac disease within 6 months: NYHA class III-IV heart failure, unstable angina or angina needing intervention, or myocardial infarction.
No contraindication to any drug in the chemotherapy regimen, including grade 2 or higher neuropathy.
No chronic strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (stopped 14 days before registration) or strong CYP3A4 inducers (stopped 14 days before treatment).

eligibility: Histologically confirmed mantle cell lymphoma with cyclin D1 expression and/or CCND1 rearrangement or t(11;14); cyclin D1/t(11;14)-negative MCL with an MCL expression profile (such as SOX11) is also eligible. Any stage (I-IV).
Measurable disease by PET or CT (liver disease must be measurable if liver is the only site), or bone marrow involvement by MCL.

No prior systemic treatment for MCL (steroids up to prednisone 100 mg/day or equivalent for up to 7 days before registration allowed), no prior radiation for stage I MCL, no prior BTK inhibitor or anti-CD20 antibody, and no prior stem cell transplant.

Age 70 or older, or age 60 to <70 with comorbidity precluding autologous transplant: EF <45%, DLCO <60% predicted, CrCl <70 but >30 mL/min, ECOG 2, or CIRS total score >6. Not a transplant candidate or declined transplant.
ECOG performance status 0-2.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

ANC 750/mm3 or more and platelets 75,000/mm3 or more (50,000/mm3 or more if due to lymphoma), without growth factor or transfusion within 7 days; CrCl 30 mL/min or more; total bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less (unless Gilbert's); AST/ALT 3 x ULN or less.

No clinically significant cardiovascular disease: unstable angina within 3 months, NYHA class III-IV heart failure, clinically significant arrhythmia (sustained VT, VF, torsades), QTcF >480 msec (unless pacemaker), or Mobitz II or third-degree block without a pacemaker.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months. No active hepatitis B or C: prior HBV exposure allowed with undetectable viral load on prophylactic antivirals; prior HCV allowed with undetectable viral load.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

No severe bleeding disorder (hemophilia A/B, von Willebrand disease, or spontaneous bleeding requiring transfusion or intervention); no stroke or intracranial hemorrhage within 6 months before registration.

No disease significantly affecting GI absorption (malabsorption, gastric or small bowel resection, bariatric surgery, symptomatic IBD, bowel obstruction); must swallow pills. Recovered from major surgery.
No live vaccine within 35 days before registration; no hypersensitivity to zanubrutinib or rituximab.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers stopped 14 days before registration.

schema.text: Stratified by ISS stage (1-2 vs 3) and cytogenetic risk (high risk: 1q gain/amplification, t(4;14), t(14;16), t(14;20), del(17p)). 56-day cycles until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

arms.text: Belantamab mafodotin 1.9 mg/kg IV day 1 plus dexamethasone 40 mg (20 mg if 75 or older) days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29, 36, 43, 50.

eligibility: Relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma by IMWG criteria, with measurable disease: serum M-protein 0.5 g/dL or more, urine M-protein 200 mg/24 h or more, or involved FLC 10 mg/dL or more with abnormal ratio.
Two or more prior lines of therapy, or triple-class exposed (exposed or refractory to an IMiD and/or PI and/or daratumumab or other anti-CD38 antibody).
No prior iberdomide, belantamab mafodotin, or other BCMA-directed therapy; no monoclonal antibody within 2 weeks; no targeted (non-antibody) or investigational agent within 2 weeks without recovery.
No severe allergic reaction (including erythema nodosum) to lenalidomide, pomalidomide, or another IMiD; no hypersensitivity to belantamab mafodotin or its components.
No prior allogeneic transplant (syngeneic allowed only without current or prior GvHD); no live vaccine within 30 days; no plasmapheresis within 7 days; no major surgery within 2 weeks.
Age 18 or older; ECOG performance status 0-2; not pregnant and not nursing.

ANC 1,000/mm3 or more; platelets 75,000/mm3 or more (50,000/mm3 or more in phase II if marrow plasma cells >50%); CrCl 30 mL/min or more (Cockcroft-Gault); spot urine albumin/creatinine <500 mg/g; bilirubin 2 x ULN or less; AST/ALT 2.5 x ULN or less; alkaline phosphatase 3 x ULN or less.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment; treated brain metastases allowed if follow-up imaging shows no progression.

No uncontrolled HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C. HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months. HCV allowed only after successful antiviral treatment with negative RNA after at least 4 weeks washout. HBcAb-positive/HBsAg-negative allowed with undetectable HBV DNA; HBsAg-positive allowed only with undetectable DNA on antivirals started at least 4 weeks before registration and no cirrhosis.

No unacceptable cardiac risk: uncontrolled arrhythmia or Mobitz II/third-degree AV block; MI, acute coronary syndrome, angioplasty, stenting, or bypass within 3 months; NYHA class III-IV heart failure; uncontrolled hypertension; congenital long QT or QTcF >480 msec; any VF or torsades; symptomatic bradycardia (HR <50); LVEF <30%.

No Child-Pugh score above 1 or cirrhosis (stable non-cirrhotic liver disease or hepatobiliary myeloma involvement allowed); no active renal condition or dialysis (isolated myeloma proteinuria allowed); no active mucosal or internal bleeding; no active infection.
No symptomatic amyloidosis, active POEMS syndrome, or active plasma cell leukemia.
No chronic strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers (stop 14 days before registration); able to swallow oral agents.

Step 2 (Arm 1 crossover): IMWG progression on belantamab/dexamethasone with measurable disease (including PET/CT or MRI progression), ANC 1,000/mm3 or more, platelets 75,000/mm3 or more (50,000/mm3 if marrow plasma cells >50%), CrCl 30 mL/min or more, bilirubin 2 x ULN or less, AST/ALT 2.5 x ULN or less.

Prior iberdomide allowed, but not iberdomide-refractory (progression on or within 60 days of stopping iberdomide).
No MM-directed therapy since ide-cel infusion; steroids for ide-cel toxicity allowed if off steroids for >30 days by C1D1.
Age 18 or older; ECOG performance status 0-2; not pregnant and not nursing.

ANC 1,500/mm3 or more; platelets 75,000/mm3 or more; CrCl 30 mL/min or more by MDRD; bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less; AST/ALT 3 x ULN or less. No platelet transfusion or growth factor to meet criteria (1 week for short-acting myeloid factors; 2 weeks for platelet or pegylated factors).
No POEMS syndrome or vital-organ amyloidosis (skin, lymph node, or incidental marrow amyloid allowed); plasma cell leukemia allowed.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated; HCV must be cured, or undetectable viral load if on treatment.
No active infection at registration (completed treatment for resolved infection and chronic maintenance antimicrobials allowed).
No known iberdomide allergy; able to swallow oral agents.

schema.label: Pre-registration
schema.text: Mandatory central pathology review and biomarker testing (MGH/DFCI) of FFPE tissue to confirm meningioma and assign a mutation-matched arm. If multiple alterations, enroll to the least common (NF2 most common, SMO least). Negative for a targetable alteration, or matching cohort closed: no registration. 1 cycle = 28 days.

schema.text: Capivasertib 480 mg PO BID, 4 days on and 3 days off each week. Cohorts by grade (I vs II/III).

schema.label: Abemaciclib expansion cohort (Group 8, added Update #18)
schema.text: NF2 mutation, CDKN2A copy number loss, or CDK4, CDK6, CCND1, CCND2, CCND3, or CCNE1 copy number gain; grade 2/3 by central review: abemaciclib 200 mg PO BID.

schema.label: Treatment and follow-up

schema.label: Primary endpoints
schema.text: PFS at 6 months and response rate per arm/cohort; the abemaciclib expansion cohort uses PFS6 as the sole primary endpoint.

eligibility: Histologically proven intracranial meningioma (any grade) by central review, with a qualifying alteration by the central lab: SMO, PTCH1, NF2, CDKN2A, AKT1, PIK3CA, or PTEN mutation; CDKN2A copy number loss; or CDK4, CDK6, CCND1, CCND2, CCND3, or CCNE1 copy number gain.

Progressive or residual measurable disease: residual disease right after surgery, or growth of 25% or more in bidimensional area between scans no more than 25 months apart (grade I requires documented pre-operative progression). Bidimensionally measurable lesion at least 10 mm in both dimensions on MRI (preferred) or CT; multifocal and spinal meningiomas allowed.

Prior RT allowed with progression after RT: at least 24 weeks from RT completion if the progressive lesion was irradiated; at least 2 weeks if the progressive lesion is outside the RT field. Abemaciclib arm: at least 28 days and full recovery from adjuvant RT.

Any number of prior therapies. No chemotherapy, cancer-directed hormonal therapy, or investigational agent within 28 days (nitrosourea or mitomycin C within 6 weeks); no concurrent meningioma-directed therapy. Abemaciclib arm: chemotherapy washout at least 28 days with recovery to grade 1 or less.
Stable steroid dose for at least 4 days; recovered to grade 1 or less from prior therapy (except alopecia and fatigue); no craniotomy within 28 days before or after registration.
Age 18 or older (30 or older for SMO/PTCH1); ECOG performance status 0-2; not pregnant and not nursing.
No metastatic (extracranial) meningioma. NF patients may have other CNS tumors (schwannoma, acoustic neuroma, ependymoma) if stable for 6 months.

No known active hepatitis B or C, Child-Pugh B or C liver disease, uncontrolled gastric ulcer (grade 3 within 28 days), uncontrolled hypertension (BP >140/90), or abdominal fistula, GI perforation, or intra-abdominal abscess within 28 days.

Labs: ANC 1,500/mm3 or more; platelets 100,000/mm3 or more; creatinine 1.5 x ULN or less or CrCl >50 mL/min; bilirubin 1.5 x ULN or less (unless Gilbert's); AST/ALT 2.5 x ULN or less; Na, K, and corrected Ca normal; QTcF <450 msec; resting heart rate 50-100 bpm.

Capivasertib arm: no major surgery within 28 days; no clinically important EKG abnormality or QT risk factors; no CABG, angioplasty, stent, MI, angina, or NYHA class II or higher heart failure within 6 months; no uncontrolled hypotension; LVEF 50% or more and within institutional normal; hemoglobin 9 g/dL or more; no 3+ proteinuria or >500 mg/24 h; no prior ILD or steroid-treated radiation pneumonitis; no prior allogeneic transplant or immunodeficiency.

Capivasertib arm diabetes rules: HbA1c <8.0%, no type 1 diabetes, no insulin, no more than two oral agents; fasting glucose <167 mg/dL with known type 2 diabetes or <126 mg/dL without. NF2 or SMO/PTCH1: no uncontrolled diabetes (HbA1c >7.5 or fasting glucose >140 mg/dL).

Abemaciclib arm: grade 2/3 by central review; hemoglobin 8 g/dL or more (transfusion allowed); no active bacterial infection needing IV antibiotics, fungal infection, or detectable viral infection (including known HIV or active hepatitis B/C); no history of cardiovascular syncope, pathologic ventricular arrhythmia, or sudden cardiac arrest.

No uncontrolled comorbidity (for example ILD, dyspnea at rest or oxygen need, major gastric or small bowel resection, Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, chronic baseline grade 2 or higher diarrhea); no allergy to compounds similar to the assigned drug.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors stopped 14 days before registration, and no strong CYP3A4 inducers or CYP2D6 substrates (capivasertib); abemaciclib: avoid CYP3A inducers and strong inhibitors.

schema.label: Pre-registration
schema.text: Central biomarker testing and histopathology review must confirm WHO grade 3 astrocytoma with intact 1p/19q, an IDH mutation, and absence of CDKN2A/B homozygous codeletion. One cycle is 28 days.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Both arms receive radiotherapy, a 4-week break, 12 months of adjuvant temozolomide with blinded daily vorasidenib or placebo, then the blinded agent alone until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Radiotherapy is 59.4 Gy in 33 fractions at 1.8 Gy per day. Temozolomide is oral, 150 mg/m2/day on days 1-5 of cycle 1 and 200 mg/m2/day on days 1-5 of later cycles. Vorasidenib or placebo is 40 mg orally once daily on days 1-28. Under age 18, the blinded dose is 40 mg if weight is at least 40 kg and 20 mg if weight is under 40 kg. Doses are from the treatment-plan table; the schema page names the agents and schedule but not the gray or milligram amounts. Real-time central imaging confirms progression. Follow-up continues for 10 years or until death.

arms.label: Control arm
arms.text: Radiotherapy, a 4-week break, then temozolomide on days 1-5 plus placebo on days 1-28 for 12 months, then placebo alone on days 1-28 until progression.

arms.label: Experimental arm
arms.text: Radiotherapy, a 4-week break, then temozolomide on days 1-5 plus vorasidenib on days 1-28 for 12 months, then vorasidenib alone on days 1-28 until progression.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival by blinded independent review, for vorasidenib plus adjuvant temozolomide after radiotherapy compared with placebo plus adjuvant temozolomide after radiotherapy, in newly diagnosed IDH-mutant WHO grade 3 astrocytoma.

eligibility: Step 0 requires a histologic diagnosis of IDH-mutant astrocytoma, CNS WHO grade 3, with diagnostic H&E and immunohistochemical slides for central review and tissue for central CDKN2A/B and 1p/19q testing, plus IDH1 or IDH2 testing if needed.
Step 1 requires central confirmation of IDH-mutant astrocytoma, CNS WHO grade 3, an IDH1 R132 or IDH2 R172 mutation, no CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion, and intact whole-arm 1p/19q.
There is no evidence of spinal or leptomeningeal disease.
No prior chemotherapy, cranial irradiation, IDH-inhibitor therapy, radiotherapy, vaccine therapy, small-molecule therapy, or laser ablation is allowed.
Diagnostic surgery, resection, or biopsy is within 8 weeks before registration, and radiotherapy plus adjuvant chemotherapy is planned.
Age is 12 or older, with ECOG performance status 2 or better or Karnofsky performance status at least 60%.

Required labs are ANC at least 1,500/mm3, hemoglobin at least 9 g/dL, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, total bilirubin at most 1.5 x ULN (at most 1.0 x ULN in Gilbert syndrome), AST and ALT at most 2.5 x ULN, alkaline phosphatase at most 2.5 x ULN, and creatinine at most 2.0 x ULN or calculated creatinine clearance greater than 40 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault at age 18 or older, Bedside Schwartz under 18).
Patients are not pregnant and not nursing, and women of childbearing potential need a negative pregnancy test within 14 days before registration.
There is no severe intercurrent illness, no active infection requiring systemic anti-infective therapy, and no unexplained fever above 38.5 degrees C within 7 days before registration.
A prior or concurrent malignancy is allowed if it would not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment, and the patient must be able to undergo MRI.

HIV is allowed on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months before registration; chronic hepatitis B must have an undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated; hepatitis C must be cured, or undetectable on current treatment.
There is no NYHA class III or IV heart failure, myocardial infarction, unstable angina, or stroke within 6 months, and patients should be class 2B or better.
There is no history of grade 2 or higher intratumoral or peritumoral hemorrhage.

Active inflammatory gastrointestinal disease, chronic diarrhea, prior gastric resection or lap-band dysphagia, short-gut syndrome, gastroparesis, or inability to swallow oral agents is excluded; treated gastroesophageal reflux is allowed.
There is no known hypersensitivity to vorasidenib or temozolomide.
No concurrent investigational agent and no concurrent alternating tumor treating fields are allowed.

Therapeutic corticosteroid doses for glioma are not allowed, physiologic steroids at or below 10 mg prednisone daily are allowed for conditions unrelated to glioma, and glioma-related corticosteroids should be the smallest dose that controls edema and stopped whenever possible.
Warfarin and other coumadin-derivative anticoagulants are not allowed and must be stopped at least 7 days before registration; low molecular weight heparin and factor Xa inhibitors are allowed.
Strong or moderate CYP1A2 inhibitors, moderate CYP1A2 inducers, and CYP3A substrates for which a small concentration change can reduce efficacy must be replaced before registration.

arms.label: Arm B (sequential)
arms.text: Platinum doublet x 4 cycles, +/- PORT, then pembrolizumab 400 mg IV every 6 weeks x 8 doses (16 cycles)

arms.label: Arm C (concurrent)
arms.text: Platinum doublet x 4 cycles with pembrolizumab 400 mg on day 1 of cycles 1 and 3, +/- PORT, then pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks x 6 doses (12 cycles), 16 total cycles of pembrolizumab

schema.label: PORT (optional)
schema.text: At treating physician discretion after the 4 chemotherapy cycles; recommended for occult pN2/N3, R1 margins, or extranodal extension, not for tumor size or pleural involvement alone. 50-54 Gy in 2 Gy (25-27 fractions) or 1.8 Gy (28-30 fractions). Starts 2-6 weeks after the last chemotherapy infusion and before continuation pembrolizumab, with no concurrent systemic therapy; pembrolizumab resumes 5-21 days after PORT.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Up to 10 years or until death. Primary endpoint DFS.

eligibility: Completely resected (R0, negative margins) stage IIA, IIB, IIIA, or IIIB (T3-4N2) NSCLC of any histology, AJCC 8th edition.
Pathologic N2 found at resection is eligible; N2 known before surgery is not.
Non-squamous: local EGFR testing with no exon 19 deletion or L858R, and local ALK testing with no rearrangement (failed ALK testing counts as negative).
Local PD-L1 IHC by DAKO 22C3, DAKO 28-8, E1L3N, or SP263.
Fully recovered from surgery; registration 30-77 days after surgery.
Age 18 or older; ECOG PS 0-1.

ANC at least 1,500/mm3, platelets at least 100,000/mm3, hemoglobin at least 8 g/dL, creatinine clearance at least 45 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault), total bilirubin up to 1.5 x ULN, AST/ALT up to 2.5 x ULN.
No prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant therapy for this lung cancer.
No current pneumonitis and no history of non-infectious pneumonitis that required steroids.
No active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment within the last 2 years (replacement therapy such as thyroxine, insulin, or physiologic corticosteroids is allowed).
No prior allogeneic tissue or solid organ transplant.
No uncontrolled intercurrent illness (active infection, symptomatic CHF, uncontrolled arrhythmia, unstable angina).
HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible. No known hepatitis C (detectable HCV RNA) or known history of hepatitis B (HBsAg reactive).

No active second malignancy that is progressing or required active treatment within the last 3 years (non-melanoma skin cancer, low-grade or low-risk cancers, stage I cancers not needing systemic therapy, and curatively treated carcinoma in situ are allowed).
No grade 3 or higher hypersensitivity to pembrolizumab or its excipients.
No live vaccine within 30 days before registration.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

schema.label: Step 1: Registration
schema.text: Stage I-IIIA pleural mesothelioma (UICC 8th edition), untreated. 1 cycle = 6 weeks.

schema.label: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy
schema.text: Nivolumab 360 mg IV on days 1 and 22 plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV on day 1 of each 6-week cycle, for 2 cycles. Then assessed for surgery.

schema.label: Step 2: Registration and surgery
schema.text: Register 21-90 days after the last immunotherapy dose. Extended pleurectomy/decortication or extrapleural pneumonectomy per surgeon, aiming for macroscopic cytoreduction, within 90 days of the last immunotherapy dose. Patients not eligible for surgery are observed and treated at physician discretion.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Up to 5 years from registration or until death. Co-primary endpoints: surgery rate after ipilimumab/nivolumab and 12-month PFS rate.

eligibility: Step 1: Pleural mesothelioma of any histology, stage I-IIIA (UICC TNM 8th edition), measurable or non-measurable disease.

Step 1: No chest wall invasion, peritoneal spread, contralateral pleural involvement, mediastinal organ involvement, vertebral involvement, contralateral intrathoracic nodal metastases, or any supraclavicular nodes.
Step 1: No prior treatment for mesothelioma and no prior hormones or chemotherapy (hormones for non-disease conditions allowed).
Step 1: Age 18 or older; ECOG PS 0-2 or Karnofsky 60% or higher.

Step 1: No active, known, or suspected autoimmune disease (vitiligo, type 1 diabetes, hypothyroidism on replacement, psoriasis not needing systemic treatment, or conditions not expected to recur without a trigger are allowed).
Step 1: No history of symptomatic interstitial lung disease.

Step 1: No active systemic infection requiring therapy and no positive hepatitis B surface antigen or hepatitis C antibody. HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible.
Step 1: No condition likely to require anti-TNF alpha or other immunosuppressive therapy during the study.
Step 1: Patients with cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better.

Step 1: Not pregnant and not nursing.

Step 2: No progression that would preclude resection; ECOG PS 0-2 or Karnofsky 60% or higher.
Step 2: Predicted FEV1 above 35% and predicted postoperative DLCO above 35%.
Step 2: Registration 21-90 days after the last immunotherapy dose.

schema.text: Completely resected pathologic stage IA3 or IB NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS ≥ 50%, registered 21-77 days after surgery. Treatment begins ≤ 14 days after registration.

arms.text: Atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-tqjs 1875 mg SC every 3 weeks (preferred) or atezolizumab 1200 mg IV every 3 weeks, 21-day cycles, for up to 1 year from randomization (maximum 17 cycles), or until unacceptable toxicity, recurrence, or new lung primary. Route is not switched once chosen.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Up to 10 years from registration for recurrence and survival.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Disease-free survival (recurrence, second lung primary, or death), intent-to-treat.

eligibility: Pathologic stage IA3 or IB NSCLC (AJCC 9th edition), any histology except tumors containing small-cell morphology.

Complete R0 resection by lobectomy or greater; sublobar resection (wedge or segmentectomy) allowed only if the tumor was ≤ 2 cm on clinical staging, with a CT chest confirming size within 60 days of surgery.
Adequate nodal sampling per Commission on Cancer 2020 standard: at least one hilar station (level 10 or higher) and at least three distinct mediastinal stations (levels 2-9).
PD-L1 TPS ≥ 50% by an FDA-approved assay (e.g., SP263, SP142, 22C3, 28-8) on surgical or biopsy specimen.
No EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation and no ALK fusion; purely squamous tumors do not require EGFR/ALK testing.
Registration no earlier than 21 days and no later than 77 days after resection, recovered from surgery.
No prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant therapy for this lung cancer.
Age ≥ 18 years; ECOG PS ≤ 2 (or Karnofsky ≥ 60%).
ANC ≥ 1,500/mm3, platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3, total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN (Gilbert syndrome < 3.0 mg/dL), AST/ALT ≤ 3 x ULN, CrCl ≥ 30 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault).
No current pneumonitis, no history of non-infectious pneumonitis requiring steroids, and no history of interstitial lung disease.
No active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment within the last 2 years (replacement therapy such as thyroid hormone, insulin, or physiologic adrenal/pituitary steroids is allowed).

No systemic corticosteroids > 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent or other immunosuppressants within 14 days before registration (inhaled, topical, ocular, intra-articular, intranasal steroids, physiologic replacement, and brief prophylactic courses allowed).
No prior allogeneic bone marrow, stem cell, or solid organ transplant; no live vaccine within 30 days before registration; no grade ≥ 3 hypersensitivity to atezolizumab or excipients.

No uncontrolled intercurrent illness, including active infection requiring systemic therapy, symptomatic CHF (NYHA ≥ III), unstable angina, or unstable arrhythmia; patients with heart failure history or prior cardiotoxic therapy must be NYHA class 2B or better.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months before registration. No active hepatitis B or C (history allowed if HBsAg negative and HCV RNA negative); no testing required without known history.
Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if its natural history or treatment will not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test ≤ 7 days before registration for women of childbearing potential).
