schema.label: Registration
schema.text: Untreated peritoneal mesothelioma with measurable disease. Treatment begins ≤ 14 days after registration.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Surgical candidate at study entry (yes vs no); histologic subtype (epithelioid vs non-epithelioid). Pocock-Simon dynamic allocation.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: 21-day cycles, 4 cycles of induction

arms.label: Regimen 1
arms.text: Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV + pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 IV + carboplatin AUC 5 IV, day 1 every 3 weeks x 4 cycles.

arms.label: Regimen 2
arms.text: Bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV + pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 IV + carboplatin AUC 5 IV, day 1 every 3 weeks x 4 cycles.

schema.label: Response assessment
schema.text: Imaging before cycle 3 and 21-28 days after cycle 4 (surgical candidates) or before cycle 5 (non-surgical).

schema.label: Surgical candidates
schema.text: Cytoreductive surgery with HIPEC 4-8 weeks after chemotherapy, then observation with imaging every 84 days for 2 years. If surgery is insufficient, aborted, or lacks cytoreductive intent, maintenance therapy may be given.

schema.label: Non-surgical candidates
schema.text: Maintenance bevacizumab 15 mg/kg ± atezolizumab 1200 mg IV every 3 weeks regardless of randomization (atezolizumab added at investigator discretion in Regimen 2), until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or 3 years from registration.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: 2 years post treatment or 3 years from registration, whichever comes first, or until death.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Best response rate by RECIST, Regimen 1 vs Regimen 2.

eligibility: Histologically or cytologically confirmed malignant peritoneal mesothelioma, previously untreated; well-differentiated papillary and multicystic mesothelioma are excluded.
Measurable disease per RECIST 1.1.
Age ≥ 18 years; ECOG PS 0-1.

Leukocytes ≥ 2,500/mm3, ANC ≥ 1,500/mm3, platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3, CrCl ≥ 45 mL/min/1.73 m2 if creatinine above normal, total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN, AST/ALT ≤ 3.0 x ULN, UPC ratio < 1 or urine protein ≤ 1+.
No prior systemic therapy for peritoneal mesothelioma; no concurrent radiotherapy.

No active or prior autoimmune disease or immune deficiency (exceptions: autoimmune hypothyroidism on replacement, controlled type 1 diabetes on insulin, limited skin-only eczema/psoriasis/vitiligo < 10% BSA on low-potency topical steroids).
No history of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, organizing pneumonia, drug-induced or idiopathic pneumonitis, and no active pneumonitis on screening chest CT.
No prior allogeneic stem cell or solid organ transplant.
CNS metastases allowed only if treated with local therapy (surgery, radiation, ablation) and steroids tapered to ≤ 10 mg prednisone equivalent.
No inadequately controlled hypertension (> 150/100 mmHg), hypertensive crisis, or hypertensive encephalopathy.
No stroke or MI within 12 months, unstable angina, NYHA class II or greater CHF, or uncontrolled arrhythmia; no significant vascular disease within 6 months; no grade 4 venous thromboembolism.
No grade ≥ 2 hemoptysis within 1 month, bleeding diathesis, or significant coagulopathy.
No abdominal fistula, GI perforation, intra-abdominal abscess, or active GI bleeding within 6 months; no non-healing wound, active ulcer, or untreated fracture.

No major surgery or significant trauma within 28 days of treatment (diagnostic laparoscopy allowed); no core biopsy or minor procedure within 7 days; vascular access device at least 2 days before treatment.
No active infection requiring IV antibiotics at start of treatment.

No immunosuppressive medication within 2 weeks before treatment (exceptions: brief or one-time steroid pulse, mineralocorticoids, steroids for COPD/asthma, low-dose steroids for orthostatic hypotension or adrenal insufficiency).

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load; HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment.
No other malignancy within 5 years except localized in situ cancer such as basal or squamous cell skin cancer.
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test ≤ 28 days before registration).

schema.text: Recurrent or metastatic incurable nasopharyngeal carcinoma after platinum-gemcitabine and PD-1/L1 blockade. Treatment begins ≤ 14 days after registration.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: 28-day cycles. Safety lead-in in the first 6 patients per arm (12 total), with accrual paused until all complete 8 weeks.

arms.text: Nivolumab 480 mg IV + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV once every 28 days (± 3 days).

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Cabozantinib 40 mg PO daily + nivolumab 480 mg IV + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV once every 28 days (± 3 days).

schema.label: Duration
schema.text: Until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Nivolumab and ipilimumab for a maximum of 2 years; cabozantinib may continue beyond 2 years per investigator.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: 2 years after treatment discontinuation or until death.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival, cabozantinib-nivolumab-ipilimumab vs nivolumab-ipilimumab.

eligibility: Histologically documented nasopharyngeal carcinoma, any WHO type (keratinizing, non-keratinizing, basaloid squamous), regardless of EBV, HPV, p16, or PD-L1 status.
Recurrent, metastatic, incurable disease previously treated with platinum-gemcitabine and PD-1/L1 blockade (first or second line), with immunotherapy part of the most recent line.
Measurable disease per RECIST 1.1 with at least one measurable lesion not previously irradiated.
No more than 2 prior lines of systemic therapy for recurrent or metastatic NPC; no prior VEGFR-targeted therapy.
Age ≥ 18 years; ECOG PS 0-2.

ANC ≥ 1,000/mm3, hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL, platelets ≥ 100,000/mm3, creatinine ≤ 1.5 mg/dL or CrCl ≥ 30 (MDRD), total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN (Gilbert < 3 mg/dL), AST/ALT ≤ 3 x ULN (≤ 5 x ULN with liver metastases).

No chemotherapy or radiotherapy within 3 weeks (6 weeks for nitrosoureas or mitomycin C) before registration; palliative limited-field RT allowed if repeat imaging shows no new bone metastases and the irradiated lesion is not a target lesion.

Recovered from prior therapy toxicity to grade ≤ 1 (except alopecia); no prior life-threatening immune-related events likely to recur (severe pneumonitis, grade 4 bullous dermatitis/DRESS, autoimmune encephalitis, transverse myelitis, myocarditis).
No active tumor bleeding or radiographic major blood vessel infiltration.

Treated brain metastases allowed if imaging 3 weeks after CNS-directed therapy shows no progression; active brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease allowed if immediate CNS treatment is not required and unlikely during cycle 1.

No active autoimmune disease or history of autoimmune disease that might recur and affect vital organs or need immunosuppression (e.g., MS, myasthenia gravis, GBS, SLE, scleroderma, IBD, SJS/TEN); vitiligo and replaced endocrinopathies allowed.

No systemic corticosteroids > 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent or other immunosuppressants within 14 days of registration (topical, inhaled, intra-articular, adrenal replacement, and brief courses allowed).

No warfarin, direct thrombin inhibitors, betrixaban, or platelet inhibitors such as clopidogrel; low-dose aspirin, LMWH, and stable rivaroxaban, edoxaban, or apixaban (without brain metastases) allowed.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load; HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment. Prior solid organ transplant allowed.
No prior malignancy whose natural history or treatment could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Able to swallow oral medication.
Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test ≤ 7 days before registration).

schema.text: Locally advanced unresectable or recurrent/metastatic adrenocortical carcinoma, age ≥ 12. Treatment begins ≤ 28 days after registration.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Prior systemic therapy (treatment naive vs ≥ 1 prior line); corticosteroid-producing tumor (yes vs no). Pocock-Simon dynamic allocation.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: 21-day cycles

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Cabozantinib 60 mg PO once daily, continuous, until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Cemiplimab 350 mg IV day 1 every 21 days + cabozantinib 40 mg PO once daily. Cemiplimab maximum 2 years; cabozantinib alone may continue afterward until progression or toxicity.

schema.label: Step 2: Crossover (Arm C)
schema.text: Arm A patients with RECIST progression may re-register within 4 weeks (± 1 week) to cemiplimab 350 mg IV every 21 days + cabozantinib daily (no re-escalation of a previously reduced cabozantinib dose); cemiplimab maximum 2 years.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Up to 4 years from registration.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Progression-free survival per RECIST 1.1, cabozantinib-cemiplimab vs cabozantinib alone.

eligibility: Histologically or cytologically confirmed adrenocortical carcinoma, locally advanced unresectable or recurrent/metastatic, with disease evaluable by RECIST 1.1.
Up to 3 prior systemic lines in the unresectable/recurrent/metastatic setting (EDP-M counts as 1 line); treatment-naive patients allowed.
No prior cabozantinib or other cMET inhibitor, anti-CTLA-4, or anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy.

Prior RT, cytotoxic chemotherapy, or targeted therapy allowed if completed ≥ 14 days before registration with toxicity recovered to grade ≤ 1; lesions irradiated within 1 month cannot be index lesions.
Mitotane within 6 months: must be stopped ≥ 28 days before registration with a mitotane level < 2 mg/L.
Age ≥ 12 years and BSA ≥ 1.2 m2. ECOG 0-2 (age ≥ 18), Lansky ≥ 50 (age 12-15), or Karnofsky ≥ 50 (age 16-17).

ANC ≥ 1,000/mcL without growth factor within 2 weeks, platelets ≥ 100,000/mcL, hemoglobin ≥ 8 g/dL, total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN (Gilbert ≤ 3 mg/dL), AST/ALT ≤ 3 x ULN, UPCR ≤ 1 mg/mg, CrCl ≥ 30 mL/min.
Adrenal steroid production assessed (random ACTH and cortisol) within 3 months before registration, for stratification.

Cardiac: NYHA class II or better if cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy; no congenital long QT, no myocarditis, no MI or unstable angina within 6 months; no uncontrolled hypertension (sustained ≥ 150/90 mmHg) within 14 days.

No GI conditions with bleeding or perforation risk within 6 months (active ulcer, bleeding endoluminal metastasis, IBD), no GI perforation within 6 months, no tumor invading the GI tract within 28 days, and no pancreatitis.
No endobronchial lesions of main or lobar bronchi, no tumor infiltrating major pulmonary vessels or encasing any major blood vessel, and no hemoptysis > 2.5 mL within 3 months.
No history of pneumonitis.

No brain metastases or cranial epidural disease unless treated with RT and/or surgery (including radiosurgery), stable ≥ 4 weeks, neurologically asymptomatic, and off corticosteroids at treatment start.
No major surgery within 2 weeks or minor surgery within 10 days; no fracture or non-healing wound within 28 days.

No active autoimmune disease or history of autoimmune disease that may recur and affect vital organs or require immunosuppression; vitiligo and replaced endocrinopathies allowed. No steroids > 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent.

No strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers (stop 14 days before), and no warfarin, direct thrombin inhibitors, betrixaban, or platelet inhibitors within 5 days; low-dose aspirin, LMWH, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, or apixaban allowed.

HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load; HCV must be cured or undetectable on treatment. Prior or concurrent malignancy allowed if it will not interfere with assessment.
Able to swallow tablets. Not pregnant and not nursing (pregnancy test ≤ 14 days before registration).

Step 2 (crossover to Arm C): RECIST progression on Arm A cabozantinib, re-registration within 4 weeks (± 1 week) of progression, all Step 1 criteria met, not discontinued from (or meeting discontinuation criteria for) cabozantinib due to toxicity, pregnancy test ≤ 14 days before re-registration.

Eligible patients are randomly assigned to one of two arms: Experimental Group A receives hypofractionated chemoradiotherapy plus concurrent tislelizumab and surufatinib, followed by consolidation therapy with tislelizumab plus surufatinib; Experimental Group B receives the same hypofractionated chemoradiotherapy plus concurrent tislelizumab alone, followed by tislelizumab consolidation.

Cycle 1 blinatumomab/nivolumab, marrow MRD, Cycle 2 blinatumomab/nivolumab, marrow MRD, end of protocol therapy. MRD < 0.01% after Cycle 1: may stop at physician discretion or proceed to Cycle 2. MRD >= 0.01%: Cycle 2.

eligibility: Age >= 1 and < 31 years at enrollment.

First relapse of CD19-positive B-ALL, and relapse blasts must express CD19: isolated bone marrow; isolated CNS (excluding known optic nerve, retinal, and CNS chloromas) and/or testicular relapse; or combined bone marrow with CNS (same exclusions) and/or testes.
Patients with Down syndrome are eligible for isolated bone marrow relapse, or combined bone marrow with CNS (excluding known optic nerve, retinal, and CNS chloromas) and/or testicular relapse.
ECOG 0, 1, or 2. Use Karnofsky if > 16 years and Lansky if <= 16 years. For developmental delay, including Down syndrome, Lansky may replace Karnofsky, but ECOG 0-2 is still required.
Eligibility laboratories within 7 calendar days before enrollment unless otherwise indicated.
Must have fully recovered from the acute toxic effects of all prior chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or radiotherapy.
Prior blinatumomab or CD19-positive chimeric antigen receptor therapy in the upfront setting is allowed if relapsed lymphoblasts retain CD19 expression. No prior hematopoietic stem cell transplant.
One intrathecal chemotherapy at relapse is allowed. If fewer than 7 days have elapsed before protocol therapy, Day 1 intrathecal methotrexate, cytarabine, or triple intrathecal may be omitted.
In the 28 days before enrollment, up to five days of post-relapse, pre-enrollment steroids and/or hydroxyurea is allowed. There is no washout for patients who relapse while receiving upfront therapy.

Down syndrome patients who received that pre-enrollment therapy and have WBC >= 30,000/µL at enrollment still receive protocol cytoreduction with vincristine and dexamethasone, and no washout is required. If WBC < 30,000/µL, a 24 hour washout is required before immunotherapy.

Renal: creatinine clearance or radioisotope GFR >= 70 mL/min/1.73 m2, or serum creatinine at or below the age and sex maximum (male/female, mg/dL): 1 to < 2 years 0.6/0.6, 2 to < 6 years 0.8/0.8, 6 to < 10 years 1/1, 10 to < 13 years 1.2/1.2, 13 to < 16 years 1.5/1.4, >= 16 years 1.7/1.4.
Cardiac: shortening fraction >= 27% by echocardiogram, or ejection fraction >= 50% by echocardiogram, cardiac MRI, or radionuclide angiogram.
Pulmonary: no dyspnea at rest, no exercise intolerance, and pulse oximetry > 94% if there is a clinical indication to measure it.

No B-lymphoblastic lymphoma, Burkitt leukemia or lymphoma, mature B-cell leukemia, Philadelphia chromosome-positive B-ALL, or ABL-class Ph-like B-ALL (rearrangements of ABL1, ABL2, CSF1R, or PDGFRB predicted sensitive to imatinib or dasatinib).
No mixed phenotype acute leukemia, Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, or MYC translocation associated with mature (Burkitt) B-cell ALL, regardless of blast immunophenotype.

No active uncontrolled infection: positive bacterial blood culture within 48 hours of enrollment; IV or oral antibiotics with continued signs or symptoms (a course may be finished if cultures have been negative for at least 48 hours and symptoms have resolved; C. difficile requires at least 72 hours of antibacterial therapy and stools at baseline); fever above 38.2°C within 48 hours with clinical signs of infection (fever attributed to tumor burden is allowed if cultures are negative for more than 48 hours); positive fungal culture within 30 days or active therapy for presumed invasive fungal infection; or active viral or protozoal infection requiring IV treatment.
No Bloom syndrome, ataxia-telangiectasia, Fanconi anemia, Kostmann syndrome, Shwachman syndrome, or any other known bone marrow failure syndrome.

No uncontrolled HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C. HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load for at least the prior 6 months is eligible. Treated hepatitis B or C with no detectable viral burden is eligible.

No significant CNS pathology that would preclude blinatumomab, including a severe neurologic disorder or autoimmune disease with CNS involvement. Seizures well controlled on stable anti-epileptic doses are eligible. Cerebrovascular ischemia or hemorrhage with residual deficits is not eligible; resolved deficits remain eligible.

No active known or suspected autoimmune disease, except type I diabetes, hypothyroidism requiring only hormone replacement, skin disorders such as vitiligo, psoriasis, or alopecia not needing systemic treatment, or conditions not expected to recur without an external trigger.

Down syndrome with known non-hematopoietic, non-CNS/testicular extramedullary (chloromatous) disease is not eligible. Group 3 and 4 patients with chloromatous disease are eligible if it is not the only site of relapse.
Females of childbearing potential need a negative pregnancy test within 7 days before enrollment. Lactating females are not eligible unless they agree not to breastfeed.

amendments.text: Amendment #2, the current version. Reopens enrollment for patients younger than 6 months with a new age-based revumenib dosing strategy, clarifies timing of eligibility labs, prohibits strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers throughout therapy, and updates dose modifications and drug monographs.

schema.label: Study entry
schema.text: Age 1 month to < 6 years, KMT2A-rearranged leukemia (diagnosed at < 2 years) that is refractory or in first marrow relapse, CNS1/CNS2, WBC < 50,000/µL. Single-arm phase 2 with a safety lead-in (RP2D) then an expansion phase.

schema.label: Regimen A (ALL, ALAL, or MPAL phenotype; investigator choice)
schema.text: Cycle 1: revumenib + 3-drug re-induction (prednisone/prednisolone BID days 1-28, vincristine days 1, 8, 15, 22, calaspargase pegol day 4, IT methotrexate days 1 and 8). Day 29 marrow, then callback for cycle 2 dose level. Cycle 2: revumenib + FLA (fludarabine and cytarabine days 1-5, ITT day 0). Early progressive disease during cycle 1 may move straight to cycle 2, then a third FLA cycle.

schema.label: Regimen B (AML phenotype, or ALL/ALAL/MPAL by investigator choice)
schema.text: Cycles 1 and 2: revumenib + FLA (fludarabine and cytarabine days 1-5, ITT).

schema.label: Revumenib dosing in combination
schema.text: Age ≥ 6 months: DL1 130 mg/m2 Q12H (DL2 160, DL0 95). Age 2 to < 6 months: 100 mg/m2 Q12H (DL0 80). Age 1 to < 2 months: 70 mg/m2 Q12H (DL0 56). Oral liquid; strong CYP3A4 inhibitors not allowed in combination cycles.

schema.label: Disease evaluation
schema.text: Marrow day 29 (re-induction) or days 29-35 by count recovery (FLA cycles; by day 36 regardless), with central MRD. Patients not meeting treatment failure criteria continue. May leave at any time for HSCT or cellular therapy.

schema.label: Revumenib monotherapy
schema.text: Up to 12 cycles while M1 marrow is maintained without Rel-M1: 160 mg/m2 Q12H for age ≥ 6 months (95 mg/m2 with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor azole); 100 mg/m2 Q12H for age 2 to < 6 months (60 mg/m2 with azole).

schema.label: Primary endpoints
schema.text: RP2D of revumenib with chemotherapy in R/R KMT2A-R ALL, and MRD-negative remission rate in patients older than 6 months at enrollment with R/R infant KMT2A-R ALL.

eligibility: Age 1 month to < 6 years at enrollment, with initial leukemia diagnosis at < 2 years.
KMT2A-rearranged ALL, ALAL, or MPAL (lineage switch to AML allowed if prior KMT2A-R ALL/ALAL/MPAL documented), with KMT2A-R confirmed by central cytogenetics/FISH review (submitted by day 10).

Primary refractory (no remission after at least 2 frontline courses; 2 courses plus 1 blinatumomab course allowed, nothing beyond) or untreated first marrow relapse (M3; M2 with 1 confirmatory test; or M1 with 2 confirmatory tests at ≥ 1%).
CNS1 or CNS2 with no neurologic signs of CNS leukemia; CNS3 may receive prior IT therapy to reach CNS1/2. Prior CNS chloroma requires no radiographic CNS disease. No isolated extramedullary leukemia.
WBC < 50,000/µL at enrollment; hydroxyurea and/or corticosteroids allowed for up to 7 days before enrollment.
Lansky ≥ 50% if age ≥ 12 months. Able to take enteral medication (PO, NG, NJ, ND, or G-tube).

Washouts: ≥ 14 days after cytotoxic therapy (≥ 7 days if relapse on maintenance); ≥ 7 days for non-myelosuppressive agents; ≥ 21 days for antibodies (blinatumomab ≥ 3 days); ≥ 84 days after allogeneic HSCT; ≥ 28 days after DLI or cellular therapy; ≥ 14 days after local XRT, ≥ 84 days after TBI, craniospinal RT, or ≥ 50% pelvis, ≥ 42 days after other substantial marrow RT. Prior FLA allowed.
Creatinine at or below age maximum (0.4 mg/dL at 1 to < 6 months, 0.5 at 6-12 months, 0.6 at 1 to < 2 years, 0.8 at 2 to < 6 years) or measured GFR/CrCl ≥ 70 mL/min/1.73 m2.
Direct bilirubin ≤ 1.5 x ULN and ALT ≤ 135 U/L, unless disease related.
Shortening fraction ≥ 27% or EF ≥ 50%, and QTcF < 450 ms (triplicate average).
No Down syndrome, bone marrow failure syndrome (Bloom, ataxia-telangiectasia, Fanconi, Kostmann, Shwachman), or secondary KMT2A-R leukemia after cytotoxic chemotherapy for a prior cancer.
No congenital long QT, CHF, or uncontrolled arrhythmia within 6 months.

No active uncontrolled infection (positive blood culture or infectious fever within 48 hours, positive fungal culture or active invasive fungal treatment within 30 days, viral or protozoal infection needing IV therapy). HIV allowed if on non-interacting antiretrovirals with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
No active acute GVHD > grade 0 or chronic GVHD > mild (skin-only exceptions); off systemic anti-GVHD agents > 7 days. No prior solid organ transplant.
No prior revumenib (other menin inhibitors allowed). No Charcot-Marie-Tooth if receiving Regimen A.
No strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or moderate/strong inducers (stopped ≥ 5 half-lives before therapy), no other investigational or anticancer agents.

schema.label: Ph+ B-ALL
schema.text: Induction Part 1 days 1-14, then Induction Part 2 plus dasatinib days 15-29. BCR::ABL1 must be confirmed by a clinically validated assay before Day 15. Dasatinib is given continuously unless otherwise noted. End-of-induction MRD (timepoint 1): CNS2 or CNS3 at end of induction is off protocol therapy. Consolidation failure (section 3.3) is off protocol therapy. Then blinatumomab block 1 plus dasatinib, blinatumomab block 2 plus dasatinib, end-of-consolidation MRD (timepoint 2), interim maintenance I with high-dose methotrexate plus dasatinib, blinatumomab block 3 plus dasatinib, delayed intensification plus dasatinib, interim maintenance II with Capizzi methotrexate plus dasatinib, and maintenance plus dasatinib. M1 marrow at end of induction proceeds when counts recover; M2 or M3 marrow proceeds immediately. M2 or M3 marrow at end of induction, or end-of-induction MRD >= 5%, should have a marrow assessment after the first blinatumomab plus TKI cycle. Persistent testicular disease: 2400 cGy testicular radiotherapy in 12 fractions. CNS3 at diagnosis that clears by end of induction: cranial radiotherapy 1800 cGy in 10 fractions during maintenance if age >= 48 months at cranial radiotherapy; cranial radiotherapy is optional for CNS3 if age < 48 months at that time.

schema.label: ABL-class Ph-like B-ALL, assigned by fusion
schema.text: Enrollment is post-induction. Imatinib (PDGFRB) or dasatinib (non-PDGFRB) may start during induction once the fusion is identified, before enrollment. M1 marrow at end of induction proceeds when counts recover; M2 or M3 proceeds immediately. Consolidation failure is off protocol therapy. Each path is blinatumomab block 1 plus TKI, blinatumomab block 2 plus TKI, end-of-consolidation MRD, interim maintenance I high-dose methotrexate plus TKI, blinatumomab block 3 plus TKI, delayed intensification plus TKI, interim maintenance II Capizzi methotrexate plus TKI, and maintenance plus TKI. Same testicular radiotherapy (2400 cGy in 12 fractions if persistent) and CNS3 cranial radiotherapy rules as the Ph+ schema (1800 cGy in 10 fractions during maintenance if >= 48 months; optional if < 48 months). M2 or M3 at end of induction, or end-of-induction MRD >= 5%, should have a marrow assessment after the first blinatumomab plus TKI cycle.

arms.label: PDGFRB ABL-class fusions
arms.text: Imatinib with each block above.

arms.label: Non-PDGFRB ABL-class fusions
arms.text: Dasatinib. The schema lists non-BCR ABL1, ABL2, or CSF1R gene fusions as examples.

eligibility: Age at enrollment is > 365 days and < 18 years at AIEOP-BFM sites, > 365 days and < 22 years at COG sites, and > 365 days and < 46 years at ALLTogether sites.

Newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome-positive or ABL-class Ph-like B-ALL, and leukemic blasts must express CD19. ABL-class fusions are rearrangements of ABL1, ABL2, CSF1R, or PDGFRB predicted to be sensitive to imatinib and/or dasatinib.

BCR::ABL1 must be documented by a clinically validated assay before study entry on Day 15 from the first vincristine dose. ABL-class rearrangements must be documented by a clinically validated assay, and the patient enrolled by Day 1 of blinatumomab block 1. Accepted methods include FISH, RT-PCR, and whole-transcriptome or panel RNA sequencing. Confirmation of the 5' fusion partner is not required.

Ph+ patients must already have started induction with vincristine, a corticosteroid, and pegaspargase or calaspargase pegol, with or without an anthracycline and/or other standard cytotoxic chemotherapy, and must not have received more than 14 days of systemic induction beginning with the first vincristine dose.
ABL-class Ph-like patients must have completed 4 or 5 weeks of multiagent Induction 1A.
Imatinib or dasatinib may have started before entry, but no more than 14 days of TKI for Ph+ B-ALL and no more than 35 days of TKI for ABL-class Ph-like B-ALL.
ECOG <= 2, or Karnofsky if > 16 years or Lansky if <= 16 years, >= 50%.
Eligibility laboratories within 7 days before enrollment. Repeat CBC with differential, bilirubin, ALT, and serum creatinine before therapy if more than 7 days have elapsed.
Clinical studies, if applicable, within 21 days before enrollment and start of therapy. Disease or staging imaging, if applicable, within 21 days.

Pediatric renal function (age 1-17 years): GFR >= 50 mL/min/1.73 m2 by bedside Schwartz estimated GFR or by measured GFR (nuclear blood sampling or small-molecule clearance). Adult renal function (age 18 years or older): creatinine clearance >= 30 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault, using a creatinine within 28 days, multiplied by 0.85 if female, with weight capped at 140% of ideal body weight.
Direct bilirubin < 2.0 mg/dL (34.2 micromoles/L), and ALT and AST <= 10 times the upper limit of normal.

Shortening fraction >= 27% by echocardiogram, or left ventricular ejection fraction >= 50% by radionuclide angiogram or echocardiogram, and QTc < 480 msec. Repeat echocardiogram and electrocardiogram are not required if they were done at or after the initial ALL diagnosis and before enrollment.
No known chronic myeloid leukemia. No ABL-class Ph-like B-ALL that is CNS2 or CNS3 at the end of induction. No ALL developing after a previous cancer treated with cytotoxic chemotherapy.
No active uncontrolled infection or active systemic illness that requires ongoing vasopressor support or mechanical ventilation. No Down syndrome.
No prior TKI before study entry except imatinib or dasatinib. No congenital long QT syndrome, history of ventricular arrhythmias, or heart block. No Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.

No significant CNS pathology that would preclude blinatumomab, including a severe neurologic disorder or autoimmune disease with CNS involvement. Seizures well controlled on stable anti-epileptic doses are eligible. Cerebrovascular ischemia or hemorrhage with residual deficits is not eligible; resolved deficits remain eligible.
HIV-infected patients are eligible if on effective antiretroviral therapy that does not interact with planned study agents and the viral load is undetectable within 6 months of treatment.

Female patients who are pregnant are not eligible (negative pregnancy test within 7 days before enrollment for females of childbearing potential). Lactating females who plan to breastfeed are not eligible.

schema.label: Step 1: Enrollment and steroid prephase
schema.text: APEC14B1 enrollment with diagnostic sample, then AALL2321 consent. Prednisone or prednisolone 20 mg/m2/dose TID days 1-7 for all patients (may extend 2 days awaiting KMT2A FISH). KMT2A status from COG-approved cytogenetics lab, entered by day 10 and centrally confirmed.

schema.label: Step 2: Callback and assignment by KMT2A status
schema.text: KMT2A-R: slot reservation, then randomization 1:1 (stratified by age at diagnosis) to Arm A or Arm B. KMT2A-germline: assigned to Arm C. The KMT2A-R safety phase cohort (venetoclax in place of cytarabine in induction, rolling six) closed with Amendment #3A; venetoclax DL2 (14 days) carried forward.

arms.label: Arm A (KMT2A-R control)
arms.text: 5-drug infant induction (35 days: daunorubicin days 1-2, cytarabine days 1-14, vincristine, dexamethasone, calaspargase pegol day 4, triple IT), blinatumomab block 1, split consolidation (cyclophosphamide/cytarabine/mercaptopurine, 2 x 14 days), MARMA, blinatumomab block 2, delayed intensification, maintenance (daily mercaptopurine, weekly oral methotrexate) to 2 years from start of MARMA.

arms.label: Arm B (KMT2A-R venetoclax)
arms.text: 4-drug induction with venetoclax days 1-14 (age-based mg/kg, replacing cytarabine), then the Arm A backbone with venetoclax added by cohort: Cohort 1 MARMA part 2 (with high-dose cytarabine); Cohort 2 consolidation; Cohort 3 consolidation and MARMA (if Cohorts 1 and 2 are safe); Cohort 4 induction only (if Cohorts 1-3 suspended).

schema.label: Arm C (KMT2A-germline, non-randomized)
schema.text: 5-drug infant induction, blinatumomab block 1, consolidation, interim maintenance I, blinatumomab block 2, delayed intensification, interim maintenance II, maintenance (COG SR-High backbone, as in AALL1731) to 2 years from start of IM I.

schema.label: Blinatumomab blocks
schema.text: 28-day continuous infusion, 15 mcg/m2/day (max 28 mcg/day); for M2/M3 marrow at end of induction, 5 mcg/m2/day days 1-7 then 15 mcg/m2/day days 8-28.

schema.label: Response gates
schema.text: CNS1 by end of induction. MRD < 1% at end of blinatumomab block 1, MRD < 0.01% by end of consolidation, and no residual non-CNS extramedullary disease at EOB1; otherwise treatment failure and off protocol therapy.

schema.label: Primary endpoints
schema.text: Safety and tolerability of venetoclax with chemotherapy and two blinatumomab blocks in infants with KMT2A-R ALL, and end-of-induction MRD-negative remission rate with vs without venetoclax (randomized).

eligibility: Enrolled on APEC14B1 and consented to eligibility screening (Part A) before treatment, with an adequate diagnostic marrow, blood (≥ 1,000/µL blasts), or leukapheresis sample.
Age 365 days or less at diagnosis, and > 36 weeks cumulative gestational age at enrollment.
Newly diagnosed CD19-positive B-ALL (2017 WHO), or acute leukemia of ambiguous lineage including MPAL with at least 50% B lineage.
No Down syndrome.
No secondary B-ALL after cytotoxic chemotherapy for a prior malignancy.

No prior cytotoxic chemotherapy, except prednisone, prednisolone, or methylprednisolone for ≤ 72 hours within 7 days before enrollment, hydroxyurea for ≤ 72 hours within 7 days, and one IT cytarabine or methotrexate within 7 days.
No dexamethasone within 28 days before protocol therapy, except a single dose around sedation for airway edema.

schema.label: Radiographic CR without normalization of markers
schema.text: Same high-dose chemotherapy with stem cell rescue consolidation: thiotepa/etoposide (28-day cycle), PBSC infusion, and craniospinal irradiation of 36 Gy plus involved-field boost to 54 Gy.

eligibility: Age >= 3 years and < 30 years at enrollment.

Newly diagnosed localized primary CNS NGGCT of the suprasellar and/or pineal region, by pathology and/or serum or CSF AFP above the institutional normal or > 10 ng/mL, or hCGβ > 100 mIU/mL, confirmed by rapid central marker screening on APEC14B1-CNS. Suprasellar, pineal, and bifocal tumors are included.

Eligible pathologic elements: endodermal sinus (yolk sac), embryonal carcinoma, choriocarcinoma, malignant or immature teratoma, and mixed germ cell tumor if those malignant elements are present. Patients with only mature teratoma are excluded. Pure germinoma admixed with mature teratoma is excluded.

Eligibility must be confirmed by rapid central imaging review on APEC14B1-CNS. Cranial MRI with and without gadolinium is required; if resected, pre-operative and post-operative brain MRI are required, and the post-operative MRI should be within 72 hours of surgery (recommended but not required after biopsy only). Spine MRI with gadolinium is required. Imaging within 31 days before enrollment (the post-operative MRI, if surgery was done).
Lumbar CSF cytology before enrollment unless medically contraindicated. If not obtained at surgery, obtain it at least 10 days after surgery and before enrollment.
CSF tumor markers with rapid central tumor marker review before enrollment unless medically contraindicated. Ventricular CSF at a diversion procedure is acceptable; lumbar CSF is preferred.
Serum AFP and hCGβ within 7 days before enrollment and start of therapy. CSF tumor markers and cytology within 31 days. Eligibility labs within 7 days.
ANC >= 1000/µL, platelets >= 100,000/µL and transfusion independent, and hemoglobin >= 8.0 g/dL (RBC transfusion allowed).

Creatinine clearance or radioisotope GFR >= 70 mL/min/1.73 m2, or serum creatinine at or below the age and sex maximum (male/female, mg/dL): 3 to < 6 years 0.8/0.8, 6 to < 10 years 1/1, 10 to < 13 years 1.2/1.2, 13 to < 16 years 1.5/1.4, >= 16 years 1.7/1.4.
Total bilirubin <= 1.5 times the upper limit of normal for age, and ALT <= 135 U/L. For this study the ALT upper limit of normal is set at 45 U/L.
Seizure disorder is allowed if the patient is on anticonvulsants and well controlled. Patients must not be in status epilepticus, coma, or assisted ventilation before enrollment.

Protocol therapy must begin within 31 days of definitive surgery or clinical diagnosis, whichever is later. If only a biopsy was done, the biopsy date is the definitive surgery date. If additional surgery follows a biopsy or incomplete resection, the date of the last resection is used.

No tumors outside the ventricles (basal ganglia or thalamus). No isolated mature teratoma with non-elevated markers at diagnosis. No prior tumor-directed therapy other than surgery and corticosteroids. No metastatic disease by MRI, lumbar CSF cytology, or intraoperative evidence of dissemination.

Pregnant patients are not eligible. Serum or urine pregnancy tests may be falsely positive because of hCGβ-secreting germ cell tumors; confirm the patient is not pregnant by institutional standards. Lactating females who plan to breastfeed are not eligible.

eligibility: Age >= 3 years and < 30 years at enrollment.

Newly diagnosed primary localized germinoma of the suprasellar and/or pineal region by pathology and/or serum and/or CSF hCGβ 5-50 mIU/mL and institutional normal AFP (or <= 10 ng/mL if no institutional normal exists), including contiguous ventricular or unifocal parenchymal extension. Histologic confirmation is not required for this group.

Also eligible without histologic confirmation: bifocal (pineal plus suprasellar) disease, or a pineal lesion with diabetes insipidus, with hCGβ <= 100 mIU/mL in serum and/or CSF and institutional normal AFP (or <= 10 ng/mL) in both serum and CSF.
hCGβ 51-100 mIU/mL in serum and/or CSF with institutional normal AFP (or <= 10 ng/mL) in both serum and CSF requires histologic confirmation of germinoma.

Germinoma of the basal ganglia and/or thalamus is eligible. Metastatic germinoma, including non-contiguous or distant disease in the brain, ventricles, or spine, is eligible. Germinoma admixed with mature teratoma is eligible.
ECOG 0, 1, or 2. Karnofsky if > 16 years and Lansky if <= 16 years.

Rapid central imaging review and rapid central tumor marker review on APEC14B1-CNS must be available before ACNS2321 entry. Cranial MRI with and without gadolinium; pre-operative and post-operative MRI if resected, post-operative MRI within 72 hours (recommended but not required after biopsy only). Spine MRI with gadolinium. Imaging within 31 days before enrollment.

Lumbar CSF cytology before enrollment unless medically contraindicated, and not before the spine MRI. If not obtained at surgery, obtain it at least 10 days after surgery. CSF tumor markers before enrollment unless contraindicated; ventricular CSF at diversion is acceptable and lumbar CSF is preferred.

Serum AFP and hCGβ within 7 days. CSF markers and cytology within 31 days. Eligibility labs within 7 days. Protocol therapy must begin no later than 31 days after definitive surgery or clinical diagnosis, whichever is later.
For solid tumors: ANC >= 1000/µL, platelets >= 100,000/µL and transfusion independent, and hemoglobin >= 8.0 g/dL (RBC transfusion allowed).

Pediatric renal function (age 3-17 years): serum creatinine at or below the age and sex maximum (male/female, mg/dL): 3 to < 6 years 0.8/0.8, 6 to < 10 years 1/1, 10 to < 13 years 1.2/1.2, 13 to < 16 years 1.5/1.4, >= 17 years 1.7/1.4; or 24-hour creatinine clearance >= 70 mL/min/1.73 m2; or measured GFR >= 50 mL/min/1.73 m2. Estimated GFR is not acceptable.

Adult renal function (age 18 years or older): creatinine clearance >= 70 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault or a 24-hour urine collection. Creatinine within 28 days, actual body weight capped at 140% of ideal body weight, minimum creatinine 0.7 mg/dL used in the estimate, multiplied by 0.85 if female.
Total bilirubin <= 1.5 times the upper limit of normal for age, and ALT <= 135 U/L. For this study the ALT upper limit of normal is set at 45 U/L.
No dyspnea at rest, no exercise intolerance, and pulse oximetry > 94% if there is a clinical indication to measure it.
Seizures are allowed if on anticonvulsants and well controlled. CNS toxicity must be <= Grade 2. Patients must not be in status epilepticus, coma, or assisted ventilation.
HIV-infected patients on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load are eligible.

No malignant elements of endodermal sinus (yolk sac), embryonal carcinoma, choriocarcinoma, or malignant or immature teratoma and mixed germ cell tumor. No isolated mature teratoma with negative tumor markers. No prior tumor-directed therapy other than surgery and corticosteroids.

Pregnant patients are not eligible. Pregnancy tests may be falsely positive because of hCGβ-secreting tumors; confirm by institutional standards. Lactating females who plan to breastfeed are not eligible.

publications.title: Androgen Deprivation therapy for Oligo-recurrent Prostate cancer in addition to radioTherapy (ADOPT): study protocol for a randomised phase III trial.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter open-label phase III trial in Dutch radiotherapy centers for oligorecurrent prostate cancer after primary local treatment, selected with PSMA PET/CT. Planned 280 patients.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Stratified by number of metastases, metastatic organ (lymph nodes or bone; bone if both), and local recurrence on PSMA PET/CT.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Eligible patients are randomized 1:1.

arms.label: MDRT
arms.text: Metastasis-directed radiotherapy alone. SBRT to all oligometastases, up to 4. If more than 2 pelvic nodes, whole-pelvic radiotherapy is recommended. A post-prostatectomy local recurrence is treated with fractionated prostate-bed radiotherapy plus SBRT or whole-pelvic radiotherapy. SBRT regimens: 7 Gy x 5 every other day, 10 Gy x 3 with 48 hours between fractions, or 12 Gy x 2 once weekly. An equivalent hypofractionated regimen with EQD2 at least 70 Gy is allowed. The alpha/beta clause is incomplete in the extracted sentence and is not restated.

arms.label: MDRT plus ADT
arms.text: The same radiotherapy plus 6 months of leuprorelin 45 mg subcutaneously once. An antiandrogen flare block may be used for at least 5 days before the agonist and not longer than 28 days. ADT starts no later than the first radiotherapy day and no earlier than 12 weeks before radiotherapy. Testosterone is checked 4 weeks after the injection. ADT is not continued past 6 months.

brief.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Janssen et al., BMC Cancer 2022 (PMID 35501744). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Histologically proven prostate adenocarcinoma with biochemical recurrence after prostatectomy (PSA above 0.1 ng/mL), radiotherapy (nadir plus 2 ng/mL or three consecutive rises, after excluding a bounce), or prostatectomy plus prostate-bed radiotherapy.

One to four bone or nodal lesions on PSMA PET/CT within 60 days before randomization, no visceral metastases. Pelvic nodal relapse at most 4 nodes (pelvis ends at the aortic bifurcation). Nodes above the bifurcation at most 3. Bone lesions at most 3.
Age above 18, WHO 0 to 2, PSA below 10 ng/mL (below 5 ng/mL if taking finasteride or dutasteride), PSA doubling time longer than 3 months, testosterone at least 1.7 nmol/L.
Excluded: prior ADT or chemotherapy for recurrence, painful metastases needing more than level 1 analgesia, and other invasive cancers except superficial non-melanoma skin cancer.

pretreatment.item: Baseline evaluation
pretreatment.note: History, prostate-cancer characteristics, PSMA PET/CT, physician- and patient-reported toxicity, quality of life, PSA, testosterone, hemoglobin, and alkaline phosphatase.

during.window: From up to 12 weeks before radiotherapy through 6 months
during.note: Arm 2 only. Toxicity scoring at week 4 of treatment is intended for whole-pelvic or prostate-bed radiotherapy.

followup.window: 1, 3, 6, 9, and 12 months, then every 6 months until 36 months or progression
followup.note: History, medication, WHO score, PSA, testosterone, hemoglobin, and alkaline phosphatase. CTCAE v4.0 and RTOG/EORTC toxicity. EORTC QLQ-PR25 and QLQ-C30.

followup.window: At biochemical progression, and at 12 and 24 months if no progression
followup.note: Biochemical progression is a PSA above the last pre-therapy value, confirmed 6 weeks later. Serious adverse events are collected until 2.5 years after treatment.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Phase 3 trial designed for overall survival in 900 men with high-risk prostate cancer. Accrual stopped early when orteronel development ended, and the trial was redesigned around a composite biochemical failure endpoint.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Risk criteria, type of radiotherapy boost, and whether androgen deprivation started before or after enrollment.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: 1:1 to standard therapy or standard therapy plus orteronel. Radiotherapy used at least 6 MV photons, IMRT to the pelvis 45 Gy in 25 fractions, then an IMRT boost of 34.2 Gy in 19 fractions or an LDR or HDR brachytherapy boost. PTV margins on pelvic and prostate CTVs were 0.5 to 1.0 cm. Daily image guidance was required. Androgen deprivation was a GnRH agonist for 24 months plus an oral antiandrogen through the end of radiotherapy.

arms.label: Standard therapy
arms.text: Androgen deprivation for 8 weeks, then dose-escalated radiotherapy with concurrent and adjuvant androgen deprivation for 24 months total.

arms.label: Standard therapy plus orteronel

followup.window: Every 3 months for 2 years, every 6 months for the next 3 years, then annually

schema.text: This paper analyzes INT-0091, INT-0154, and AEWS0031. Enrollment was 2001 to 2005.

schema.label: Regimen
schema.text: The standard doses stated for these studies were VCD, vincristine 2 mg/m2 (maximum 2 mg), doxorubicin 75 mg/m2, and cyclophosphamide 1200 mg/m2 with mesna, alternating with ifosfamide 1800 mg/m2/day for 5 days with mesna and etoposide 100 mg/m2/day for 5 days. Local control was after 12 weeks. Radiotherapy alone treated the initial tumor volume plus a 3 cm margin to 4500 cGy, then the postchemotherapy volume for 1080 cGy more (5580 cGy total). Microscopic residual disease was limited to 4500 cGy to the original volume plus a 1 cm margin. Completely resected tumors with clear margins received no supplemental radiotherapy.

registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: Concurrent chemo-radiotherapy is a common and conventional method of treating locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). In locally advanced HNSCC it has been proved to be superior to radiotherapy alone. On the other side accelerated fractionation radiotherapy (AFRT) is a proven practice to improve cure rate in head and neck cancers. Yet it has not been compared with Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in locally advanced HNSCC and hence this study is aiming to compare CRT versus AFRT.

arms.label: CONCURRENT CHEMO-RADIOTHERAPY ARM
arms.text: Patients assigned to CRT arm will be given radiation one fraction per day, on five consecutive days from Monday to Friday along with intravenous cisplatin 40 mg/m2 weekly for seven doses (a minimum of 5weekly chemotherapy).

arms.label: ACCELERATED FRACTIONATION RADIOTHERAPY ARM
arms.text: Patients assigned to AFRT arm will undergo radiation similarly one fraction per day and then the sixth fraction will be given on another day (Saturday) or as an extra fraction on one of the first five days, but always allowing at least a 6-hour interval between fractions on same day. If any unintended interruption of the treatment occurs, this missing treatment will be given as soon as possible, preferably within a week, but not allowing more than 14 Gy to be given during any 7-day period.

schema.label: Primary endpoints
schema.text: Low Risk: 2-year OS of at least 95.7% for stage I MGCT and at least 88% for ovarian immature teratoma with surgery plus surveillance. Standard Risk: EFS with carboplatin- vs cisplatin-based therapy (CEb vs PEb in SR1, BEC vs BEP in SR2).

eligibility: Low Risk: no age limit. SR1: age < 11 years. SR2: age ≥ 11 and < 25 years.

Newly diagnosed extracranial GCT: stage I for Low Risk strata, malignant GCT stage II or higher for Standard Risk, with histology and stage as defined per stratum (yolk sac component must be more than microscopic when it is the only malignant element).

Histologic confirmation required, except recurrence of resected non-seminoma with markers > 5 x ULN on 2 measurements at least 1 week apart, or markers AFP ≥ 500 ng/mL or HCG ≥ 500 IU/L with typical imaging when biopsy or upfront resection is not appropriate.
SR2 testicular: IGCCC good risk using post-op markers (AFP < 1,000 ng/mL, β-HCG < 5,000 mIU/mL, LDH < 3.0 x normal).
ECOG 0-3 equivalent (Karnofsky if > 16 years, Lansky if ≤ 16).

Standard Risk only: CrCl or GFR ≥ 70 mL/min/1.73 m2 or creatinine at or below the age/sex maximum; total bilirubin ≤ 2 x ULN and AST/ALT ≤ 3 x ULN (unless Gilbert's, liver involvement, or vanishing bile duct syndrome); ANC ≥ 750/mm3 and platelets ≥ 75,000/mm3.
No pure ovarian or extragonadal dysgerminoma/seminoma, pure mature teratoma, primary CNS GCT, or GCT with somatic malignant transformation.
No poor-risk GCT (age ≥ 11 with COG stage IV ovarian, stage II-IV extragonadal, or IGCCC intermediate/poor risk testicular).
No prior radiation therapy, except CNS irradiation of brain metastases in SR1 patients.
Standard Risk: no significant pre-existing respiratory disease contraindicating bleomycin.
Standard Risk: not pregnant and not breastfeeding.

eligibility: Age 5 to 60 years at enrollment.

Newly diagnosed, untreated, histologically confirmed classic Hodgkin lymphoma (nodular sclerosis, mixed cellularity, lymphocyte-rich, lymphocyte-depleted, or not otherwise specified) with stage I or II disease.
Bidimensionally measurable disease, at least one lesion with longest diameter >= 1.5 cm.
Whole body or limited whole body PET within 42 days before enrollment. PET-CT is strongly preferred. PET-MRI is allowed if intravenous contrast-enhanced CT is also obtained.

Pediatric patients age 5-17 years with known or suspected mediastinal disease must have an upright PA chest radiograph for bulk assessment. If both CT chest and upright PA chest radiograph were done, bulk may be met by either modality.
Age >= 18 years: Zubrod 0, 1, or 2. Age <= 17 years: Lansky >= 50.

Eligibility laboratories within 28 days before enrollment unless otherwise indicated. Repeat CBC with differential, bilirubin, ALT, creatinine, ESR, and, for known infections, HIV, HBV, and HCV if more than 28 days have elapsed before therapy.
Clinical studies, if applicable, within 42 days before enrollment and start of therapy. Disease or staging imaging, if applicable, within 42 days.

Pediatric renal function (age 5-17 years): serum or plasma creatinine at or below the age and sex maximum (male/female, mg/dL): 2 to < 6 years 0.8/0.8, 6 to < 10 years 1/1, 10 to < 13 years 1.2/1.2, 13 to < 16 years 1.5/1.4, >= 16 years 1.7/1.4; or 24-hour creatinine clearance >= 50 mL/min/1.73 m2; or measured GFR >= 50 mL/min/1.73 m2. Estimated GFR is not acceptable.

Adult renal function (age 18 years or older): creatinine clearance >= 30 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault or a 24-hour urine collection, creatinine within 28 days, actual body weight capped at 140% of ideal body weight, multiplied by 0.85 if female.

Total bilirubin <= 2 times the upper limit of normal, and AST and ALT <= 3 times the upper limit of normal, unless due to Gilbert disease, lymphomatous involvement of the liver, or vanishing bile duct syndrome.
Shortening fraction >= 27% by echocardiogram, MUGA, or functional cardiac imaging, or ejection fraction >= 50% by radionuclide angiogram, echocardiogram, MUGA, or cardiac imaging.
DLCO >= 50% of predicted, corrected for hemoglobin. If PFTs cannot be obtained, pulse oximetry > 92% on room air.

Known HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible. Chronic HBV must have an undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy if indicated. HCV must have been treated and cured, or, if currently treated, the HCV viral load must be undetectable.
No nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma. No history of active interstitial pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease.
No poorly controlled inherited or acquired immunodeficiency requiring active medications, such as a primary immunodeficiency syndrome, and no organ transplant recipients.

No known uncontrolled intercurrent illness that would jeopardize safety, including infection, autoimmune conditions, cardiac arrhythmias, angina pectoris, and gastrointestinal disorders affecting swallowing or absorption of pills.

No systemic corticosteroids or other immunosuppressive medications within 14 days before enrollment. The corticosteroid threshold is equivalent to > 10 mg daily prednisone for age >= 18 years, or > 0.5 mg/kg (up to 10 mg/day) for age < 18 years. Thyroxine, insulin, and physiologic adrenal or pituitary replacement are allowed. Inhaled or topical steroids and adrenal replacement doses at or below those thresholds are allowed if there is no active autoimmune disease. Steroids for Hodgkin lymphoma symptoms are allowed but must stop by Cycle 1, Day 1.
No peripheral neuropathy > Grade 1 at enrollment and no known Charcot-Marie-Tooth syndrome.
No prior or concurrent malignancy whose natural history or treatment could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment of the regimen.

No prior chemotherapy, radiation, or antibody-based treatment for classic Hodgkin lymphoma. No prior solid organ transplant. No prior allogeneic stem cell transplantation. No live vaccine within 30 days before planned Day 1 of protocol therapy. mRNA vaccines are permitted.

Pregnant patients are not eligible. A pregnancy test within 28 days before enrollment is required for females of childbearing potential. Lactating females who plan to breastfeed from the first dose through at least 6 months after the last treatment are not eligible.
